<li value="1"><style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r1041539562">.mw-parser-output .citation{word-wrap:break-word}.mw-parser-output .citation:target{background-color:rgba(0,127,255,0.133)}</style><span class="citation wikicite" id="endnote_area"><b><a href="#ref_area">^</a></b></span>  20,770&#160;km<sup>2</sup> is Israel within the <a href="/wiki/Green_Line_(Israel)" title="Green Line (Israel)">Green Line</a>. 22,072&#160;km<sup>2</sup> includes the occupied <a href="/wiki/Golan_Heights" title="Golan Heights">Golan Heights</a> (c. 1,200&#160;km<sup>2</sup> (460&#160;sq&#160;mi)) and <a href="/wiki/East_Jerusalem" title="East Jerusalem">East Jerusalem</a> (c. 64&#160;km<sup>2</sup> (25&#160;sq&#160;mi))</li>
</ol></div></td></tr></tbody></table>
<p><b>Israel</b> (<span class="rt-commentedText nowrap"><span class="IPA nopopups noexcerpt" lang="en-fonipa"><a href="/wiki/Help:IPA/English" title="Help:IPA/English">/<span style="border-bottom:1px dotted"><span title="/ˈ/: primary stress follows">ˈ</span><span title="/ɪ/: &#39;i&#39; in &#39;kit&#39;">ɪ</span><span title="&#39;z&#39; in &#39;zoom&#39;">z</span><span title="&#39;r&#39; in &#39;rye&#39;">r</span><span title="/i/: &#39;y&#39; in &#39;happy&#39;">i</span><span title="/./: syllable break">.</span><span title="/ə/: &#39;a&#39; in &#39;about&#39;">ə</span><span title="&#39;l&#39; in &#39;lie&#39;">l</span></span>,<span class="wrap"> </span>-<span style="border-bottom:1px dotted"><span title="&#39;r&#39; in &#39;rye&#39;">r</span><span title="/eɪ/: &#39;a&#39; in &#39;face&#39;">eɪ</span></span>-/</a></span></span>; <a href="/wiki/Hebrew_language" title="Hebrew language">Hebrew</a>: <span lang="he" dir="rtl">יִשְׂרָאֵל</span> <span title="Hebrew-language romanization"><i lang="he-Latn">Yīsrāʾēl</i></span> <small></small><span title="Representation in the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA)" class="IPA" lang="he-Latn-fonipa"><a href="/wiki/Help:IPA/Hebrew" title="Help:IPA/Hebrew">[jisʁaˈʔel]</a></span>; <a href="/wiki/Arabic_language" class="mw-redirect" title="Arabic language">Arabic</a>: <span lang="ar" dir="rtl">إِسْرَائِيل</span> <span title="Arabic-language romanization"><i lang="ar-Latn">ʾIsrāʾīl</i></span>), officially the <b>State of Israel</b> (<span title="Hebrew-language text"><span lang="he" dir="rtl">מְדִינַת יִשְׂרָאֵל</span></span> <span title="Hebrew-language romanization"><i lang="he-Latn">Medīnat Yīsrāʾēl</i></span> <small></small><span title="Representation in the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA)" class="IPA" lang="he-Latn-fonipa"><a href="/wiki/Help:IPA/Hebrew" title="Help:IPA/Hebrew">[mediˈnat jisʁaˈʔel]</a></span>; <span title="Arabic-language text"><span lang="ar" dir="rtl">دَوْلَة إِسْرَائِيل</span></span> <span title="Arabic-language romanization"><i lang="ar-Latn">Dawlat Isrāʾīl</i></span>), is a country in <a href="/wiki/West_Asia" title="West Asia">West Asia</a>. It is <a href="/wiki/Borders_of_Israel" title="Borders of Israel">bordered</a> by <a href="/wiki/Lebanon" title="Lebanon">Lebanon</a> to the north, by <a href="/wiki/Syria" title="Syria">Syria</a> to the northeast, by <a href="/wiki/Jordan" title="Jordan">Jordan</a> to the east, by the <a href="/wiki/Red_Sea" title="Red Sea">Red Sea</a> to the south, by <a href="/wiki/Egypt" title="Egypt">Egypt</a> to the southwest, by the <a href="/wiki/Mediterranean_Sea" title="Mediterranean Sea">Mediterranean Sea</a> to the west, and by the <a href="/wiki/Palestinian_territories" title="Palestinian territories">Palestinian territories</a>&#160;&#8211;&#32; the <a href="/wiki/West_Bank" title="West Bank">West Bank</a> along the east and the <a href="/wiki/Gaza_Strip" title="Gaza Strip">Gaza Strip</a> along the southwest. <a href="/wiki/Tel_Aviv" title="Tel Aviv">Tel Aviv</a> is the <a href="/wiki/Economy_of_Israel" title="Economy of Israel">economic</a> and <a href="/wiki/Science_and_technology_in_Israel" title="Science and technology in Israel">technological center</a> of the country, while its seat of government is in its proclaimed capital of <a href="/wiki/Jerusalem" title="Jerusalem">Jerusalem</a>, although Israeli sovereignty over <a href="/wiki/East_Jerusalem" title="East Jerusalem">East Jerusalem</a> is <a href="/wiki/Status_of_Jerusalem" title="Status of Jerusalem">unrecognized internationally</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-22" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-22">&#91;18&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-23" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-23">&#91;fn 5&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Israel is located in the <a href="/wiki/Southern_Levant" title="Southern Levant">Southern Levant</a>, a region known historically as <a href="/wiki/Canaan" title="Canaan">Canaan</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Land_of_Israel" title="Land of Israel">Land of Israel</a>, <a href="/wiki/Palestine_(region)" title="Palestine (region)">Palestine</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Holy_Land" title="Holy Land">Holy Land</a>. In the early first millennium BCE, the <a href="/wiki/Israelites" title="Israelites">Israelite</a> kingdoms of <a href="/wiki/History_of_ancient_Israel_and_Judah" title="History of ancient Israel and Judah">Israel and Judah</a> emerged, before falling to the <a href="/wiki/Neo-Assyrian_Empire" title="Neo-Assyrian Empire">Neo-Assyrian</a> and <a href="/wiki/Neo-Babylonian_empire" class="mw-redirect" title="Neo-Babylonian empire">Neo-Babylonian empires</a>, respectively.<sup id="cite_ref-Broshi_2001_174_24-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Broshi_2001_174-24">&#91;19&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-25" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-25">&#91;20&#93;</a></sup> During the <a href="/wiki/Classical_era" class="mw-redirect" title="Classical era">classical era</a>, the region was ruled by the <a href="/wiki/Achaemenid_Empire" title="Achaemenid Empire">Achaemenid</a>, <a href="/wiki/Macedonian_Empire" class="mw-redirect" title="Macedonian Empire">Macedonian</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ptolemaic_Kingdom" title="Ptolemaic Kingdom">Ptolemaic</a> and <a href="/wiki/Seleucid_Empire" title="Seleucid Empire">Seleucid</a> empires. In the 2nd century BCE, an independent <a href="/wiki/Hasmonean" class="mw-redirect" title="Hasmonean">Hasmonean</a> kingdom emerged, before <a href="/wiki/Ancient_Rome" title="Ancient Rome">Rome</a> conquered the area a century later. In the 7th century CE, the <a href="/wiki/Muslim_conquest_of_the_Levant" title="Muslim conquest of the Levant">Muslim conquest of the Levant</a> established <a href="/wiki/Caliphate" title="Caliphate">caliphal rule</a>. The <a href="/wiki/First_Crusade" title="First Crusade">First Crusade</a> of the 11th century brought the founding of <a href="/wiki/Crusader_states" title="Crusader states">Crusader states</a>, the last ending in the 13th century at the hands of the <a href="/wiki/Mamluks" class="mw-redirect" title="Mamluks">Mamluks</a>, who <a href="/wiki/Ottoman%E2%80%93Mamluk_War_(1516%E2%80%931517)" title="Ottoman–Mamluk War (1516–1517)">lost the area</a> to the <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_Empire" title="Ottoman Empire">Ottoman Empire</a> at the onset of the 16th century. In the late 19th century, Jews <a href="/wiki/Aliyah" title="Aliyah">began immigrating</a> to the area as part of the <a href="/wiki/Zionist" class="mw-redirect" title="Zionist">Zionist</a> movement. After <a href="/wiki/World_War_I" title="World War I">World War I</a>, the <a href="/wiki/San_Remo_conference" title="San Remo conference">allied powers assigned</a> the <a href="/wiki/Mandate_for_Palestine" title="Mandate for Palestine">Mandate for Palestine</a> to Britain, which during the war made a <a href="/wiki/Balfour_Declaration" title="Balfour Declaration">declaration of support</a> for the establishment of <a href="/wiki/Homeland_for_the_Jewish_people" title="Homeland for the Jewish people">a national home for the Jewish people in Palestine</a>. Following <a href="/wiki/World_War_II" title="World War II">World War II</a> and <a href="/wiki/The_Holocaust" title="The Holocaust">the Holocaust</a>, the newly formed <a href="/wiki/United_Nations" title="United Nations">United Nations</a> adopted the <a href="/wiki/United_Nations_Partition_Plan_for_Palestine" title="United Nations Partition Plan for Palestine">Partition Plan for Palestine</a>, recommending the creation of independent Arab and Jewish states, and <a href="/wiki/Corpus_separatum_(Jerusalem)" title="Corpus separatum (Jerusalem)">placing Jerusalem under international control</a>. In the final months of the <a href="/wiki/Mandatory_Palestine" title="Mandatory Palestine">British Mandate</a>, a <a href="/wiki/1947%E2%80%931948_civil_war_in_Mandatory_Palestine" title="1947–1948 civil war in Mandatory Palestine">civil war</a> broke out between the Palestinian Arabs and the <a href="/wiki/Yishuv" title="Yishuv">Yishuv</a>, beginning the first stage of the <a href="/wiki/1948_Palestine_war" title="1948 Palestine war">1948 Palestine war</a>. The British terminated the Mandate on 14 May 1948, and Israel <a href="/wiki/Israeli_Declaration_of_Independence" title="Israeli Declaration of Independence">declared independence</a> that day.
</p><p>Upon its independence, Israel became almost immediately embroiled in conflict with its five neighboring Arab states, whose armies began entering the area of the former Mandatory Palestine on 15 May, starting the <a href="/wiki/1948_Arab%E2%80%93Israeli_War" title="1948 Arab–Israeli War">1948 Arab–Israeli War</a>. Early the next year, the <a href="/wiki/1949_Armistice_Agreements" title="1949 Armistice Agreements">1949 Armistice Agreements</a> left Israel in control of over one-third more territory than the partition plan had called for, with no independent Arab state created. During both stages of the 1948 Palestine war, over <a href="/wiki/1948_Palestinian_expulsion_and_flight" title="1948 Palestinian expulsion and flight">700,000 Palestinian Arabs were expelled from or fled</a> Israeli territory to the <a href="/wiki/Jordanian_annexation_of_the_West_Bank" title="Jordanian annexation of the West Bank">West Bank</a>, <a href="/wiki/All-Palestine_Protectorate" title="All-Palestine Protectorate">Gaza</a>, and the neighboring Arab countries, with fewer than 150,000 Palestinian Arabs remaining within Israel. During and immediately after the war, around 260,000 <a href="/wiki/Jewish_exodus_from_Arab_and_Muslim_lands" class="mw-redirect" title="Jewish exodus from Arab and Muslim lands">Jews emigrated or fled from the Arab world</a> to Israel.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEFischbach200826–27_26-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFischbach200826–27-26">&#91;21&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-27" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-27">&#91;fn 6&#93;</a></sup> The 1967 <a href="/wiki/Six-Day_War" title="Six-Day War">Six-Day War</a> resulted in the <a href="/wiki/Israeli_occupation_of_the_West_Bank" title="Israeli occupation of the West Bank">Israeli occupation of the West Bank</a> and Gaza Strip, along with the Egyptian <a href="/wiki/Sinai_Peninsula" title="Sinai Peninsula">Sinai Peninsula</a> and the Syrian <a href="/wiki/Golan_Heights" title="Golan Heights">Golan Heights</a>. Israel has since effectively annexed both <a href="/wiki/Israeli_annexation_of_East_Jerusalem" title="Israeli annexation of East Jerusalem">East Jerusalem</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Golan_Heights_Law" title="Golan Heights Law">Golan Heights</a>, and has established <a href="/wiki/Israeli_settlements" class="mw-redirect" title="Israeli settlements">settlements</a> across the Israeli-occupied territories, actions the international community has rejected as illegal under international law. Israel has signed peace treaties <a href="/wiki/Camp_David_Accords" title="Camp David Accords">with Egypt</a>, returning the Sinai Peninsula, and <a href="/wiki/Israel%E2%80%93Jordan_peace_treaty" title="Israel–Jordan peace treaty">with Jordan</a>, and more recently <a href="/wiki/Abraham_Accords" title="Abraham Accords">normalized relations with several Arab countries</a>, though efforts to resolve the Israeli–Palestinian conflict have not succeeded. Israel's practices in its occupation of the Palestinian territories, the longest military occupation in modern history, have <a href="/wiki/List_of_United_Nations_resolutions_concerning_Israel" title="List of United Nations resolutions concerning Israel">drawn international condemnation</a> for violating the human rights of the Palestinians, including <a href="/wiki/Israel_and_apartheid" title="Israel and apartheid">accusations of apartheid</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-28" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-28">&#91;22&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The country has a <a href="/wiki/Parliamentary_system" title="Parliamentary system">parliamentary system</a>, <a href="/wiki/Proportional_representation" title="Proportional representation">proportional representation</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Universal_suffrage" title="Universal suffrage">universal suffrage</a>. The <a href="/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Israel" title="Prime Minister of Israel">prime minister</a> serves as head of <a href="/wiki/Cabinet_of_Israel" title="Cabinet of Israel">government</a>, and is elected by the <a href="/wiki/Knesset" title="Knesset">Knesset</a>, Israel's <a href="/wiki/Unicameralism" title="Unicameralism">unicameral legislature</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-cnn_29-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cnn-29">&#91;23&#93;</a></sup> Israel is a <a href="/wiki/Developed_country" title="Developed country">developed country</a> and an <a href="/wiki/OECD" title="OECD">OECD</a> member,<sup id="cite_ref-OECD_30-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-OECD-30">&#91;24&#93;</a></sup> with a <a href="/wiki/Demographics_of_Israel" title="Demographics of Israel">population of over 9 million people</a> as of 2021<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Israel&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup>.<sup id="cite_ref-31" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-31">&#91;25&#93;</a></sup> It has the world's <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_GDP_(nominal)" title="List of countries by GDP (nominal)">29th-largest economy by nominal GDP</a> and <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_GDP_(nominal)_per_capita" title="List of countries by GDP (nominal) per capita">13th by nominal GDP per capita</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-IMFWEOIL_19-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-IMFWEOIL-19">&#91;15&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" />
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Etymology"><span class="anchor" id="Etymology"></span> Etymology</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Names_of_Israel#Israel_and_Judea" class="mw-redirect" title="Names of Israel">Names of Israel</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Merenptah_Israel_Stele_Cairo.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/Merenptah_Israel_Stele_Cairo.jpg/150px-Merenptah_Israel_Stele_Cairo.jpg" decoding="async" width="150" height="235" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/Merenptah_Israel_Stele_Cairo.jpg/225px-Merenptah_Israel_Stele_Cairo.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/Merenptah_Israel_Stele_Cairo.jpg/300px-Merenptah_Israel_Stele_Cairo.jpg 2x" data-file-width="491" data-file-height="768" /></a><figcaption>The <a href="/wiki/Merneptah_Stele" title="Merneptah Stele">Merneptah Stele</a> (13th century BCE). The majority of <a href="/wiki/Biblical_Archeology" class="mw-redirect" title="Biblical Archeology">biblical archeologists</a> translate a set of hieroglyphs as "Israel", the first instance of the name in the record.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Under the <a href="/wiki/Mandate_for_Palestine" title="Mandate for Palestine">British Mandate</a> (1920–1948), the whole region was known as 'Palestine' (<a href="/wiki/Hebrew_language" title="Hebrew language">Hebrew</a>: <span lang="he" dir="rtl">פלשתינה [א״י]</span>, <small><a href="/wiki/Literal_translation" title="Literal translation">lit.</a>&#8201;</small>&#39;Palestine [Eretz Israel]&#39;).<sup id="cite_ref-32" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-32">&#91;26&#93;</a></sup> Upon <a href="/wiki/Israeli_Declaration_of_Independence" title="Israeli Declaration of Independence">independence</a> in 1948, the country formally adopted the name 'State of Israel' (<a href="/wiki/Hebrew_language" title="Hebrew language">Hebrew</a>: <span lang="he" dir="rtl">מְדִינַת יִשְׂרָאֵל</span>, <span data-nosnippet="" id="ooui-php-1" class="ext-phonos ext-phonos-PhonosButton noexcerpt oo-ui-widget oo-ui-widget-enabled oo-ui-buttonElement oo-ui-buttonElement-frameless oo-ui-iconElement oo-ui-labelElement oo-ui-buttonWidget" data-ooui="{&quot;_&quot;:&quot;mw.Phonos.PhonosButton&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;\/\/upload.wikimedia.org\/wikipedia\/commons\/transcoded\/2\/2b\/He-Medinat_Israel2.ogg\/He-Medinat_Israel2.ogg.mp3&quot;,&quot;rel&quot;:[&quot;nofollow&quot;],&quot;framed&quot;:false,&quot;icon&quot;:&quot;volumeUp&quot;,&quot;label&quot;:{&quot;html&quot;:&quot;&lt;span title=\&quot;Hebrew-language romanization\&quot;&gt;&lt;i lang=\&quot;he-Latn\&quot;&gt;&lt;i&gt;Med\u012bnat Yisr\u0101&#39;el&lt;\/i&gt;&lt;\/i&gt;&lt;\/span&gt;&quot;},&quot;data&quot;:{&quot;ipa&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;text&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;lang&quot;:&quot;en&quot;,&quot;wikibase&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;file&quot;:&quot;He-Medinat class="oo-ui-iconElement-icon oo-ui-icon-volumeUp"></span><span class="oo-ui-labelElement-label"><span title="Hebrew-language romanization"><i lang="he-Latn"><i>Medīnat Yisrā'el</i></i></span></span><span class="oo-ui-indicatorElement-indicator oo-ui-indicatorElement-noIndicator"></span></a></span><sup class="ext-phonos-attribution noexcerpt"><a href="/wiki/File:He-Medinat_Israel2.ogg" title="File:He-Medinat Israel2.ogg">i</a></sup> <small></small><span title="Representation in the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA)" class="IPA" lang="he-Latn-fonipa"><a href="/wiki/Help:IPA/Hebrew" title="Help:IPA/Hebrew">[mediˈnat jisʁaˈʔel]</a></span>; <a href="/wiki/Arabic_language" class="mw-redirect" title="Arabic language">Arabic</a>: <span lang="ar" dir="rtl">دَوْلَة إِسْرَائِيل</span>, <span title="American Library Association – Library of Congress transliteration"><i lang="ar-Latn"><i>Dawlat Isrāʼīl</i></i></span>, <small></small><span title="Representation in the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA)" class="IPA" lang="ar-Latn-fonipa"><a href="/wiki/Help:IPA/Arabic" title="Help:IPA/Arabic">[dawlat ʔisraːˈʔiːl]</a></span>) after other <a href="/wiki/Israeli_Declaration_of_Independence#Name" title="Israeli Declaration of Independence">proposed historical and religious names</a> including '<a href="/wiki/Land_of_Israel" title="Land of Israel">Land of Israel</a>' (<i>Eretz Israel</i>), Ever (from ancestor <a href="/wiki/Eber" title="Eber">Eber</a>), <a href="/wiki/Zion" title="Zion">Zion</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Judea" title="Judea">Judea</a>, were considered but rejected,<sup id="cite_ref-33" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-33">&#91;27&#93;</a></sup> while the name 'Israel' was suggested by <a href="/wiki/Ben-Gurion" class="mw-redirect" title="Ben-Gurion">Ben-Gurion</a> and passed by a vote of 6–3.<sup id="cite_ref-34" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-34">&#91;28&#93;</a></sup> In the early weeks of independence, the government chose the term "<a href="/wiki/Israelis" title="Israelis">Israeli</a>" to denote a citizen of Israel, with the formal announcement made by <a href="/wiki/Foreign_Affairs_Minister_of_Israel" class="mw-redirect" title="Foreign Affairs Minister of Israel">Minister of Foreign Affairs</a> <a href="/wiki/Moshe_Sharett" title="Moshe Sharett">Moshe Sharett</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-35" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-35">&#91;29&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The names <a href="/wiki/Land_of_Israel" title="Land of Israel">Land of Israel</a> and <a href="/wiki/Children_of_Israel" class="mw-redirect" title="Children of Israel">Children of Israel</a> have historically been used to refer to the biblical <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Israel_(united_monarchy)" title="Kingdom of Israel (united monarchy)">Kingdom of Israel</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Jewish_people" class="mw-redirect" title="Jewish people">entire Jewish people</a> respectively.<sup id="cite_ref-levine_36-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-levine-36">&#91;30&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Israel_(name)" title="Israel (name)">name 'Israel'</a> (Hebrew:&#160;<i>Yisraʾel</i>, <i>Isrāʾīl</i>; <a href="/wiki/Septuagint" title="Septuagint">Septuagint</a> <a href="/wiki/Greek_language" title="Greek language">Greek</a>: <span lang="el">Ἰσραήλ</span>, <i>Israēl</i>, 'El (God) persists/rules', though after <a rel="nofollow" class="external text" href="https://bible.oremus.org/?passage=Hosea%2012:4&amp;version=nrsv">Hosea 12:4</a> often interpreted as 'struggle with God')<sup id="cite_ref-37" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-37">&#91;31&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-38" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-38">&#91;32&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-39" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-39">&#91;33&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-40" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-40">&#91;34&#93;</a></sup> in these phrases refers to the patriarch <a href="/wiki/Jacob" title="Jacob">Jacob</a> who, according to the <a href="/wiki/Hebrew_Bible" title="Hebrew Bible">Hebrew Bible</a>, was given the name after he successfully wrestled with the angel of the Lord.<sup id="cite_ref-41" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-41">&#91;35&#93;</a></sup> Jacob's twelve sons became the ancestors of the <a href="/wiki/Israelites" title="Israelites">Israelites</a>, also known as the <i><a href="/wiki/Twelve_Tribes_of_Israel" title="Twelve Tribes of Israel">Twelve Tribes of Israel</a></i> or <i>Children of Israel</i>. Jacob and his sons had lived in <a href="/wiki/Canaan" title="Canaan">Canaan</a> but were forced by famine to go into <a href="/wiki/Egypt" title="Egypt">Egypt</a> for four generations, lasting 430 years,<sup id="cite_ref-42" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-42">&#91;36&#93;</a></sup> until <a href="/wiki/Moses" title="Moses">Moses</a>, a great-great-grandson of Jacob,<sup id="cite_ref-43" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-43">&#91;37&#93;</a></sup> led the Israelites back into <a href="/wiki/Canaan" title="Canaan">Canaan</a> during the "<a href="/wiki/The_Exodus" title="The Exodus">Exodus</a>". The earliest known archaeological artefact to mention the word "Israel" as a collective is the <a href="/wiki/Merneptah_Stele" title="Merneptah Stele">Merneptah Stele</a> of <a href="/wiki/Ancient_Egypt" title="Ancient Egypt">ancient Egypt</a> (dated to the late 13th century BCE).<sup id="cite_ref-44" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-44">&#91;38&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="History">History</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/History_of_Israel" title="History of Israel">History of Israel</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">For a chronological guide, see <a href="/wiki/Timeline_of_Israeli_history" title="Timeline of Israeli history">Timeline of Israeli history</a>.</div>
<p><a href="/wiki/Early_expansions_of_hominins_out_of_Africa" title="Early expansions of hominins out of Africa">Early expansions of hominins out of Africa</a> into the <a href="/wiki/Prehistory_of_the_Levant" title="Prehistory of the Levant">prehistoric Levant</a>, where Israel is located, dates back at least 1.5 <a href="/wiki/Million_years_ago" class="mw-redirect" title="Million years ago">million years ago</a> based on traces found at <a href="/wiki/Ubeidiya_prehistoric_site" title="Ubeidiya prehistoric site">Ubeidiya</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Jordan_Rift_Valley" title="Jordan Rift Valley">Jordan Rift Valley</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-45" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-45">&#91;39&#93;</a></sup> while the <a href="/wiki/Skhul_and_Qafzeh_hominins" title="Skhul and Qafzeh hominins">Skhul and Qafzeh hominins</a>, <i><a href="/wiki/Homo_sapiens" class="mw-redirect" title="Homo sapiens">Homo sapiens</a></i> fossils dating back 120,000 years, are some of the earliest traces of <a href="/wiki/Anatomically_modern_human" class="mw-redirect" title="Anatomically modern human">anatomically modern humans</a> outside of Africa.<sup id="cite_ref-46" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-46">&#91;40&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Natufian_culture" title="Natufian culture">Natufian culture</a> emerged in the <a href="/wiki/Southern_Levant" title="Southern Levant">southern Levant</a> by the 10th millennium BCE,<sup id="cite_ref-47" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-47">&#91;41&#93;</a></sup> followed by the <a href="/wiki/Ghassulian" title="Ghassulian">Ghassulian</a> culture by around 4,500 BCE.<sup id="cite_ref-48" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-48">&#91;42&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Bronze_and_Iron_Ages">Bronze and Iron Ages</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/History_of_ancient_Israel_and_Judah" title="History of ancient Israel and Judah">History of ancient Israel and Judah</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Canaan" title="Canaan">Canaan</a>, <a href="/wiki/Israelites" title="Israelites">Israelites</a>, <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Israel_(Samaria)" title="Kingdom of Israel (Samaria)">Kingdom of Israel (Samaria)</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Judah" title="Kingdom of Judah">Kingdom of Judah</a></div><figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:JW_IMG_4893.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/JW_IMG_4893.JPG/180px-JW_IMG_4893.JPG" decoding="async" width="180" height="240" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/JW_IMG_4893.JPG/270px-JW_IMG_4893.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/JW_IMG_4893.JPG/360px-JW_IMG_4893.JPG 2x" data-file-width="2736" data-file-height="3648" /></a><figcaption>Canaanite <a href="/wiki/Walls_of_Jerusalem" title="Walls of Jerusalem">wall of Jerusalem</a> in the <a href="/wiki/City_of_David_(archaeological_site)" title="City of David (archaeological site)">City of David</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/Canaan" title="Canaan">Canaanites</a> are archaeologically attested in the <a href="/wiki/Middle_bronze_age" class="mw-redirect" title="Middle bronze age">Middle Bronze Age</a> (2100–1550 BCE).<sup id="cite_ref-Golden_49-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Golden-49">&#91;43&#93;</a></sup> During the <a href="/wiki/Late_Bronze_Age" class="mw-redirect" title="Late Bronze Age">Late Bronze Age</a> (1550–1200 BCE), large parts of Canaan formed <a href="/wiki/Vassal_state" title="Vassal state">vassal states</a> paying tribute to the <a href="/wiki/New_Kingdom_of_Egypt" title="New Kingdom of Egypt">New Kingdom of Egypt</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-50" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-50">&#91;44&#93;</a></sup> As a result of the <a href="/wiki/Late_Bronze_Age_collapse" title="Late Bronze Age collapse">Late Bronze Age collapse</a>, Canaan fell into chaos, and Egyptian control over the region collapsed completely.<sup id="cite_ref-51" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-51">&#91;45&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-52" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-52">&#91;46&#93;</a></sup> There is evidence that urban centers such as <a href="/wiki/Tel_Hazor" title="Tel Hazor">Hazor</a>, <a href="/wiki/Beit_She%27an" title="Beit She&#39;an">Beit She'an</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tel_Megiddo" title="Tel Megiddo">Megiddo</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ekron" title="Ekron">Ekron</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ashdod" title="Ashdod">Ashdod</a> and <a href="/wiki/Ashkelon" title="Ashkelon">Ashkelon</a> were damaged or destroyed.<sup id="cite_ref-53" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-53">&#91;47&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>A people named Israel appear for the first time in the <a href="/wiki/Merneptah_Stele" title="Merneptah Stele">Merneptah Stele</a>, an <a href="/wiki/Ancient_Egypt" title="Ancient Egypt">ancient Egyptian</a> inscription which dates to about 1200 BCE.<sup id="cite_ref-NollMerneptah_54-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NollMerneptah-54">&#91;48&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-ThompsonMerneptah_55-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ThompsonMerneptah-55">&#91;49&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-56" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-56">&#91;50&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-57" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-57">&#91;51&#93;</a></sup> Ancestors of the <a href="/wiki/Israelites" title="Israelites">Israelites</a> are thought to have included <a href="/wiki/Ancient_Semitic-speaking_peoples" title="Ancient Semitic-speaking peoples">ancient Semitic-speaking peoples</a> native to this area.<sup id="cite_ref-Miller1986_58-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Miller1986-58">&#91;52&#93;</a></sup><sup class="reference nowrap"><span title="Page / location: 78–79">&#58;&#8202;78–79&#8202;</span></sup> According to the modern archaeological account, the Israelites and their culture branched out of the Canaanite peoples and their cultures through the development of a distinct <a href="/wiki/Monolatry" title="Monolatry">monolatristic</a>—and later <a href="/wiki/Monotheism" title="Monotheism">monotheistic</a>—religion centered on <a href="/wiki/Yahweh" title="Yahweh">Yahweh</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-59" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-59">&#91;53&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-60" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-60">&#91;54&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-61" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-61">&#91;55&#93;</a></sup> They spoke an archaic form of the <a href="/wiki/Hebrew_language" title="Hebrew language">Hebrew language</a>, known as <a href="/wiki/Biblical_Hebrew" title="Biblical Hebrew">Biblical Hebrew</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-62" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-62">&#91;56&#93;</a></sup> Around the same time, the <a href="/wiki/Philistines" title="Philistines">Philistines</a> settled on the southern <a href="/wiki/Israeli_coastal_plain" title="Israeli coastal plain">coastal plain</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEKillebrew2005230_63-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKillebrew2005230-63">&#91;57&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEShahin20056_64-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShahin20056-64">&#91;58&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Modern <a href="/wiki/Archaeology" title="Archaeology">archaeology</a> has largely discarded <a href="/wiki/Historicity_of_the_Bible" title="Historicity of the Bible">the historicity</a> of the narrative in the <a href="/wiki/Torah" title="Torah">Torah</a> concerning the <a href="/wiki/Patriarchs_(Bible)" title="Patriarchs (Bible)">patriarchs</a>, <a href="/wiki/The_Exodus" title="The Exodus">The Exodus</a> and the tales of conquest described in the <a href="/wiki/Book_of_Joshua" title="Book of Joshua">Book of Joshua</a>, and instead views the narrative as constituting the Israelites' <a href="/wiki/National_myth" title="National myth">national myth</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-65" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-65">&#91;59&#93;</a></sup> However, some elements of these traditions do appear to have historical roots.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEFaust2015p.476:_&quot;While_there_is_a_consensus_among_scholars_that_the_Exodus_did_not_take_place_in_the_manner_described_in_the_Bible,_surprisingly_most_scholars_agree_that_the_narrative_has_a_historical_core,_and_that_some_of_the_highland_settlers_came,_one_way_or_another,_from_Egypt..&quot;_66-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFaust2015p.476:_&quot;While_there_is_a_consensus_among_scholars_that_the_Exodus_did_not_take_place_in_the_manner_described_in_the_Bible,_surprisingly_most_scholars_agree_that_the_narrative_has_a_historical_core,_and_that_some_of_the_highland_settlers_came,_one_way_or_another,_from_Egypt..&quot;-66">&#91;60&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERedmount200161_67-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERedmount200161-67">&#91;61&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:03_68-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:03-68">&#91;62&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Kingdoms_of_Israel_and_Judah_map_830.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/Kingdoms_of_Israel_and_Judah_map_830.svg/170px-Kingdoms_of_Israel_and_Judah_map_830.svg.png" decoding="async" width="170" height="203" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/Kingdoms_of_Israel_and_Judah_map_830.svg/255px-Kingdoms_of_Israel_and_Judah_map_830.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/Kingdoms_of_Israel_and_Judah_map_830.svg/340px-Kingdoms_of_Israel_and_Judah_map_830.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="720" data-file-height="859" /></a><figcaption>Map of <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Israel_(Samaria)" title="Kingdom of Israel (Samaria)">Israel</a> and <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Judah" title="Kingdom of Judah">Judah</a> in the 9th century BCE</figcaption></figure>
<p>There is debate about the earliest existence of the <a href="/wiki/History_of_ancient_Israel_and_Judah" title="History of ancient Israel and Judah">Kingdoms of Israel and Judah</a> and their extent and power. While it is unclear if there was ever a <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Israel_(united_monarchy)" title="Kingdom of Israel (united monarchy)">United Kingdom of Israel</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-lipschits_69-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-lipschits-69">&#91;63&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Kuhrtp438_70-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Kuhrtp438-70">&#91;64&#93;</a></sup> historians and archaeologists agree that the northern <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Israel_(Samaria)" title="Kingdom of Israel (Samaria)">Kingdom of Israel</a> existed by <abbr title="circa">ca.</abbr> 900 BCE<sup id="cite_ref-Finkelstein_71-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Finkelstein-71">&#91;65&#93;</a></sup><sup class="reference nowrap"><span title="Page / location: 169–195">&#58;&#8202;169–195&#8202;</span></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Wright_72-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Wright-72">&#91;66&#93;</a></sup> and that the <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Judah" title="Kingdom of Judah">Kingdom of Judah</a> existed by <abbr title="circa">ca.</abbr> 850 BCE.<sup id="cite_ref-Finkelstein,_Israel,_(2020)_73-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Finkelstein,_Israel,_(2020)-73">&#91;67&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Pitcher_74-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Pitcher-74">&#91;68&#93;</a></sup> The Kingdom of Israel was the more prosperous of the two kingdoms and soon developed into a regional power;<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEFinkelsteinSilberman2002146–7_75-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFinkelsteinSilberman2002146–7-75">&#91;69&#93;</a></sup> during the days of the <a href="/wiki/Omride_Dynasty" class="mw-redirect" title="Omride Dynasty">Omride dynasty</a>, it controlled <a href="/wiki/Samaria" title="Samaria">Samaria</a>, <a href="/wiki/Galilee" title="Galilee">Galilee</a>, the upper <a href="/wiki/Jordan_Valley" title="Jordan Valley">Jordan Valley</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Sharon_plain" title="Sharon plain">Sharon</a> and large parts of the <a href="/wiki/Transjordan_(region)" title="Transjordan (region)">Transjordan</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-:0_76-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-76">&#91;70&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Samaria_(ancient_city)" title="Samaria (ancient city)">Samaria</a>, the capital, was home to one of the largest Iron Age structures in the Levant.<sup id="cite_ref-:04_77-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:04-77">&#91;71&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-78" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-78">&#91;72&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The Kingdom of Israel was destroyed around 720 BCE, when it was conquered by the <a href="/wiki/Neo-Assyrian_Empire" title="Neo-Assyrian Empire">Neo-Assyrian Empire</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Broshi_2001_174_24-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Broshi_2001_174-24">&#91;19&#93;</a></sup> The Kingdom of Judah, with its capital in <a href="/wiki/Jerusalem" title="Jerusalem">Jerusalem</a>, later became a <a href="/wiki/Client_state" title="Client state">client state</a> of first the Neo-Assyrian Empire and then the <a href="/wiki/Neo-Babylonian_Empire" title="Neo-Babylonian Empire">Neo-Babylonian Empire</a>. It is estimated that <a href="/wiki/Demographic_history_of_Palestine_(region)" title="Demographic history of Palestine (region)">the region's population</a> was around 400,000 in the <a href="/wiki/Iron_Age_II" class="mw-redirect" title="Iron Age II">Iron Age II</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-:42_79-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:42-79">&#91;73&#93;</a></sup> In 587/6 BCE, following a <a href="/wiki/Judah%27s_revolts_against_Babylon" title="Judah&#39;s revolts against Babylon">revolt in Judah</a>, King <a href="/wiki/Nebuchadnezzar_II" title="Nebuchadnezzar II">Nebuchadnezzar II</a> <a href="/wiki/Siege_of_Jerusalem_(587_BC)" title="Siege of Jerusalem (587 BC)">besieged and destroyed Jerusalem</a> and Solomon's Temple,<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEFinkelsteinSilberman2002307_80-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFinkelsteinSilberman2002307-80">&#91;74&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-81" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-81">&#91;75&#93;</a></sup> dissolved the kingdom and exiled much of the Judean elite to <a href="/wiki/Babylon" title="Babylon">Babylon</a>, beginning the <a href="/wiki/Babylonian_captivity" title="Babylonian captivity">Babylonian captivity</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-82" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-82">&#91;76&#93;</a></sup> The defeat was also recorded in the <a href="/wiki/Babylonian_Chronicles" title="Babylonian Chronicles">Babylonian Chronicles</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-BabylonianChronicles_83-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-BabylonianChronicles-83">&#91;77&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-84" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-84">&#91;78&#93;</a></sup> After <a href="/wiki/Fall_of_Babylon" title="Fall of Babylon">capturing Babylon</a> in 539 BCE, <a href="/wiki/Cyrus_the_Great" title="Cyrus the Great">Cyrus the Great</a>, founder of the <a href="/wiki/Achaemenid_Empire" title="Achaemenid Empire">Persian Achaemenid Empire</a>, issued a <a href="/wiki/Edict_of_Cyrus" title="Edict of Cyrus">proclamation</a> allowing the exiled Judean population to return to Judah.<sup id="cite_ref-rennert_85-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-rennert-85">&#91;79&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-86" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-86">&#91;80&#93;</a></sup> The returned Jewish population was permitted to self-govern and rebuild the Temple.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Classical_antiquity">Classical antiquity</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Second_Temple_period" title="Second Temple period">Second Temple period</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Yehud_(province)" class="mw-redirect" title="Yehud (province)">Yehud (province)</a>, <a href="/wiki/Hasmonean_dynasty" title="Hasmonean dynasty">Hasmonean dynasty</a>, <a href="/wiki/Herodian_dynasty" title="Herodian dynasty">Herodian dynasty</a>, <a href="/wiki/Judaea_(Roman_province)" title="Judaea (Roman province)">Judaea (Roman province)</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Syria_Palaestina" title="Syria Palaestina">Syria Palaestina</a></div>
<p>The construction of the <a href="/wiki/Second_Temple" title="Second Temple">Second Temple</a> was completed <abbr title="circa">c.</abbr><span style="white-space:nowrap;">&#8201;520 BCE</span>.<sup id="cite_ref-rennert_85-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-rennert-85">&#91;79&#93;</a></sup> The Persians ruled the region as the province of <a href="/wiki/Yehud_(Persian_province)" class="mw-redirect" title="Yehud (Persian province)">Yehud</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-Grabbe355_87-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Grabbe355-87">&#91;81&#93;</a></sup> which had a population of around 30,000 people in the 5th to 4th centuries BCE.<sup id="cite_ref-Finkelstein_71-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Finkelstein-71">&#91;65&#93;</a></sup><sup class="reference nowrap"><span title="Page / location: 308">&#58;&#8202;308&#8202;</span></sup>
</p><p>In 332 BCE, <a href="/wiki/Alexander_the_Great" title="Alexander the Great">Alexander the Great</a> of <a href="/wiki/Macedonia_(ancient_kingdom)" title="Macedonia (ancient kingdom)">Macedon</a> conquered the region as part of his <a href="/wiki/Wars_of_Alexander_the_Great" title="Wars of Alexander the Great">campaign against the Persian Empire</a>. After his death, the area was controlled by the <a href="/wiki/Ptolemaic_Kingdom" title="Ptolemaic Kingdom">Ptolemaic</a> and <a href="/wiki/Seleucid_Empire" title="Seleucid Empire">Seleucid</a> empires as a part of <a href="/wiki/Coele-Syria" title="Coele-Syria">Coele-Syria</a>. Over the ensuing centuries, the <a href="/wiki/Hellenization" title="Hellenization">Hellenization</a> of the region led to cultural tensions that came to a head during the reign of <a href="/wiki/Antiochus_IV_Epiphanes" title="Antiochus IV Epiphanes">Antiochus IV</a>, giving rise to the <a href="/wiki/Maccabean_Revolt" title="Maccabean Revolt">Maccabean Revolt</a> of 167 BCE. The civil unrest weakened Seleucid rule and in the late 2nd century the semi-autonomous <a href="/wiki/Hasmonean_dynasty" title="Hasmonean dynasty">Hasmonean Kingdom of Judea</a> arose, eventually attaining full independence and expanding into neighboring regions.<sup id="cite_ref-88" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-88">&#91;82&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-89" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-89">&#91;83&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-90" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-90">&#91;84&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Israel-2013-Aerial_21-Masada.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/14/Israel-2013-Aerial_21-Masada.jpg/180px-Israel-2013-Aerial_21-Masada.jpg" decoding="async" width="180" height="240" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/14/Israel-2013-Aerial_21-Masada.jpg/270px-Israel-2013-Aerial_21-Masada.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/14/Israel-2013-Aerial_21-Masada.jpg/360px-Israel-2013-Aerial_21-Masada.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3755" data-file-height="5000" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Masada" title="Masada">Masada</a> fortress, the location of a <a href="/wiki/Siege_of_Masada" title="Siege of Masada">1st-century Roman siege</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/Roman_Republic" title="Roman Republic">Roman Republic</a> invaded the region in 63 BCE, first <a href="/wiki/Third_Mithridatic_War" title="Third Mithridatic War">taking control of Syria</a>, and then intervening in the <a href="/wiki/Hasmonean_Civil_War" title="Hasmonean Civil War">Hasmonean Civil War</a>. The <a href="/wiki/Roman%E2%80%93Parthian_Wars" title="Roman–Parthian Wars">struggle</a> between pro-Roman and pro-<a href="/wiki/Parthian_Empire" title="Parthian Empire">Parthian</a> factions in Judea led to the installation of <a href="/wiki/Herod_the_Great" title="Herod the Great">Herod the Great</a> as a <a href="/wiki/Herodian_dynasty" title="Herodian dynasty">dynastic</a> <a href="/wiki/Vassal_state" title="Vassal state">vassal</a> of <a href="/wiki/Ancient_Rome" title="Ancient Rome">Rome</a>. In 6 CE, the area was fully annexed as the <a href="/wiki/Judea_(Roman_province)" class="mw-redirect" title="Judea (Roman province)">Roman province of Judaea</a>, a period that heralded tensions with Roman rule, and led to a series of <a href="/wiki/Jewish%E2%80%93Roman_wars" title="Jewish–Roman wars">Jewish–Roman wars</a>, resulting in widespread destruction. The <a href="/wiki/First_Jewish%E2%80%93Roman_War" title="First Jewish–Roman War">First Jewish-Roman War</a> (66–73 CE) resulted in the <a href="/wiki/Siege_of_Jerusalem_(70_CE)" title="Siege of Jerusalem (70 CE)">destruction of Jerusalem and the Second Temple</a> and a sizable portion of the population being killed or displaced.<sup id="cite_ref-:8_91-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:8-91">&#91;85&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>A second uprising known as the <a href="/wiki/Bar_Kokhba_revolt" title="Bar Kokhba revolt">Bar Kokhba revolt</a> took place during 132–136 CE. Initial successes allowed the Jews to form an independent state in Judea, but the Romans massed large forces and brutally crushed the rebellion, devastating and depopulating Judea's countryside.<sup id="cite_ref-:8_91-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:8-91">&#91;85&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-92" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-92">&#91;86&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-93" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-93">&#91;87&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:02_94-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:02-94">&#91;88&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-95" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-95">&#91;89&#93;</a></sup> Jerusalem was rebuilt as a <a href="/wiki/Colonia_(Roman)" title="Colonia (Roman)">Roman colony</a> under the name of <a href="/wiki/Aelia_Capitolina" title="Aelia Capitolina">Aelia Capitolina</a>, and the province of Judea was renamed <a href="/wiki/Syria_Palaestina" title="Syria Palaestina">Syria Palaestina</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-H.H._Ben-Sasson,_1976,_page_334_96-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-H.H._Ben-Sasson,_1976,_page_334-96">&#91;90&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Ariel_Lewin_p._33_97-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ariel_Lewin_p._33-97">&#91;91&#93;</a></sup> Jews were expelled from the districts surrounding Jerusalem,<sup id="cite_ref-98" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-98">&#91;92&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:02_94-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:02-94">&#91;88&#93;</a></sup> and joined communities in the diaspora.<sup id="cite_ref-Kessler20102_99-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Kessler20102-99">&#91;93&#93;</a></sup> Nevertheless, there was a continuous small Jewish presence and <a href="/wiki/Galilee" title="Galilee">Galilee</a> became its religious center.<sup id="cite_ref-100" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-100">&#91;94&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-101" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-101">&#91;95&#93;</a></sup> Jewish communities also continued to reside in the southern <a href="/wiki/Hebron_Hills" title="Hebron Hills">Hebron Hills</a> and on the coastal plain.<sup id="cite_ref-:02_94-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:02-94">&#91;88&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Late_antiquity_and_the_medieval_period">Late antiquity and the medieval period</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Diocese_of_the_East" title="Diocese of the East">Diocese of the East</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bilad_al-Sham" title="Bilad al-Sham">Bilad al-Sham</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Jerusalem" title="Kingdom of Jerusalem">Kingdom of Jerusalem</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Ruins_of_the_Ancient_Synagogue_at_Bar%27am.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e0/Ruins_of_the_Ancient_Synagogue_at_Bar%27am.jpg/220px-Ruins_of_the_Ancient_Synagogue_at_Bar%27am.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e0/Ruins_of_the_Ancient_Synagogue_at_Bar%27am.jpg/330px-Ruins_of_the_Ancient_Synagogue_at_Bar%27am.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e0/Ruins_of_the_Ancient_Synagogue_at_Bar%27am.jpg/440px-Ruins_of_the_Ancient_Synagogue_at_Bar%27am.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4048" data-file-height="3040" /></a><figcaption>3rd-century <a href="/wiki/Kfar_Bar%27am_synagogue" title="Kfar Bar&#39;am synagogue">Kfar Bar'am synagogue</a> in the Galilee<sup id="cite_ref-102" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-102">&#91;96&#93;</a></sup></figcaption></figure>
<p>With the transition of Roman rule into that of the <a href="/wiki/Byzantine_Empire" title="Byzantine Empire">Byzantine Empire</a> under <a href="/wiki/Emperor_Constantine" class="mw-redirect" title="Emperor Constantine">Emperor Constantine</a>, <a href="/wiki/Early_Christianity" title="Early Christianity">Early Christianity</a> displaced the more tolerant <a href="/wiki/Roman_Paganism" class="mw-redirect" title="Roman Paganism">Roman Paganism</a> as an external influence.<sup id="cite_ref-103" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-103">&#91;97&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:3_104-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:3-104">&#91;98&#93;</a></sup> With the <a href="/wiki/Conversion_of_Constantine" class="mw-redirect" title="Conversion of Constantine">conversion of Constantine</a> in the 4th century, the situation for the Jewish majority in Palestine "became more difficult".<sup id="cite_ref-Kessler20102_99-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Kessler20102-99">&#91;93&#93;</a></sup> A series of laws were passed that discriminated against Jews and Judaism, and Jews were persecuted by both the church and the authorities.<sup id="cite_ref-:3_104-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:3-104">&#91;98&#93;</a></sup> Many Jews had emigrated to flourishing <a href="/wiki/Jewish_diaspora" title="Jewish diaspora">Diaspora</a> communities,<sup id="cite_ref-:1_105-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-105">&#91;99&#93;</a></sup> while locally there was both Christian immigration and local conversion. By the middle of the 5th century, there was a Christian majority.<sup id="cite_ref-CHJ2_106-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-CHJ2-106">&#91;100&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-107" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-107">&#91;101&#93;</a></sup> Towards the end of the 5th century, <a href="/wiki/Samaritan_revolts" title="Samaritan revolts">Samaritan revolts</a> erupted, continuing until the late 6th century and resulting in a large decrease in the Samaritan population.<sup id="cite_ref-108" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-108">&#91;102&#93;</a></sup> After the <a href="/wiki/Sasanian_conquest_of_Jerusalem" title="Sasanian conquest of Jerusalem">Sasanian conquest of Jerusalem</a> and the short-lived <a href="/wiki/Jewish_revolt_against_Heraclius" title="Jewish revolt against Heraclius">Jewish revolt against Heraclius</a> in 614 CE, the Byzantine Empire <a href="/wiki/Byzantine%E2%80%93Sasanian_War_of_602%E2%80%93628" title="Byzantine–Sasanian War of 602–628">reconsolidated control of the area</a> in 628.<sup id="cite_ref-109" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-109">&#91;103&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 634–641 CE, the <a href="/wiki/Rashidun_Caliphate" title="Rashidun Caliphate">Rashidun Caliphate</a> <a href="/wiki/Muslim_conquest_of_the_Levant" title="Muslim conquest of the Levant">conquered the Levant</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-:12_110-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:12-110">&#91;104&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-111" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-111">&#91;105&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:102_112-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:102-112">&#91;106&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:Ellenblum20102_113-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:Ellenblum20102-113">&#91;107&#93;</a></sup> Over the next six centuries, control of the region transferred between the <a href="/wiki/Umayyad" class="mw-redirect" title="Umayyad">Umayyad</a>, <a href="/wiki/Abbasid_Caliphate" title="Abbasid Caliphate">Abbasid</a>, <a href="/wiki/Fatimid_Caliphate" title="Fatimid Caliphate">Fatimid</a> <a href="/wiki/Caliphate" title="Caliphate">caliphates</a>, and subsequently the <a href="/wiki/Seljuks" class="mw-redirect" title="Seljuks">Seljuks</a> and <a href="/wiki/Ayyubid_dynasty" title="Ayyubid dynasty">Ayyubid</a> dynasties.<sup id="cite_ref-MosheGil2_114-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-MosheGil2-114">&#91;108&#93;</a></sup> The population of the area drastically decreased during the following several centuries, dropping from an estimated 1 million during Roman and Byzantine periods to about 300,000 by the early Ottoman period. Alongside this population decline, there was a steady process of <a href="/wiki/Arabization" title="Arabization">Arabization</a> and <a href="/wiki/Islamization" class="mw-redirect" title="Islamization">Islamization</a> brought on by non-Muslim emigration, Muslim immigration, and local conversion to Islam.<sup id="cite_ref-:Ellenblum20102_113-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:Ellenblum20102-113">&#91;107&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:102_112-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:102-112">&#91;106&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:Broshi1979_115-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:Broshi1979-115">&#91;109&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:43_116-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:43-116">&#91;110&#93;</a></sup> The end of the 11th century brought the <a href="/wiki/Crusades" title="Crusades">Crusades</a>, <a href="/wiki/The_Pope" class="mw-redirect" title="The Pope">papally</a>-sanctioned incursions of Christian <a href="/wiki/Crusaders" class="mw-redirect" title="Crusaders">crusaders</a> intent on wresting <a href="/wiki/Jerusalem" title="Jerusalem">Jerusalem</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Holy_Land" title="Holy Land">Holy Land</a> from Muslim control and establishing <a href="/wiki/Crusader_States" class="mw-redirect" title="Crusader States">Crusader States</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-117" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-117">&#91;111&#93;</a></sup> The Ayyubids pushed back the crusaders before Muslim rule was fully restored by the <a href="/wiki/Mamluk_Sultanate_(Cairo)" class="mw-redirect" title="Mamluk Sultanate (Cairo)">Mamluk sultans of Egypt</a> in 1291.<sup id="cite_ref-GudrunKramer2_118-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-GudrunKramer2-118">&#91;112&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Modern_period_and_the_emergence_of_Zionism">Modern period and the emergence of Zionism</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_Syria" title="Ottoman Syria">Ottoman Syria</a>, <a href="/wiki/Jerusalem_Sanjak" title="Jerusalem Sanjak">Jerusalem Sanjak</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Mutasarrifate_of_Jerusalem" title="Mutasarrifate of Jerusalem">Mutasarrifate of Jerusalem</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Old_Yishuv" title="Old Yishuv">Old Yishuv</a> and <a href="/wiki/Zionism" title="Zionism">Zionism</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Jews_at_Western_Wall_by_Felix_Bonfils,_1870s.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5b/Jews_at_Western_Wall_by_Felix_Bonfils%2C_1870s.jpg/220px-Jews_at_Western_Wall_by_Felix_Bonfils%2C_1870s.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="171" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5b/Jews_at_Western_Wall_by_Felix_Bonfils%2C_1870s.jpg/330px-Jews_at_Western_Wall_by_Felix_Bonfils%2C_1870s.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5b/Jews_at_Western_Wall_by_Felix_Bonfils%2C_1870s.jpg/440px-Jews_at_Western_Wall_by_Felix_Bonfils%2C_1870s.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2978" data-file-height="2313" /></a><figcaption>Jews at the <a href="/wiki/Western_Wall" title="Western Wall">Western Wall</a> in the 1870s</figcaption></figure>
<p>In 1516, the region was conquered by the <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_Empire" title="Ottoman Empire">Ottoman Empire</a> and proceeded to be ruled as a part of <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_Syria" title="Ottoman Syria">Ottoman Syria</a> for the next four centuries. In 1660, a <a href="/wiki/Druze_power_struggle_(1658%E2%80%931667)#Lebanon_and_Galilee_campaign" title="Druze power struggle (1658–1667)">Druze revolt</a> led to the destruction of <a href="/wiki/1660_destruction_of_Safed" title="1660 destruction of Safed">Safed</a> and <a href="/wiki/1660_destruction_of_Tiberias" title="1660 destruction of Tiberias">Tiberias</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-119" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-119">&#91;113&#93;</a></sup> In the late 18th century, local Arab <a href="/wiki/Sheikh" title="Sheikh">Sheikh</a> <a href="/wiki/Zahir_al-Umar" title="Zahir al-Umar">Zahir al-Umar</a> created a de facto independent Emirate in the Galilee. Ottoman attempts to subdue the Sheikh failed, but after Zahir's death the Ottomans regained control of the area. In 1799 governor <a href="/wiki/Jazzar_Pasha" title="Jazzar Pasha">Jazzar Pasha</a> successfully repelled an <a href="/wiki/Siege_of_Acre_(1799)" title="Siege of Acre (1799)">assault on Acre</a> by troops of <a href="/wiki/Napoleon" title="Napoleon">Napoleon</a>, prompting the French to abandon the Syrian campaign.<sup id="cite_ref-120" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-120">&#91;114&#93;</a></sup> In 1834, a <a href="/wiki/Peasants%27_revolt_in_Palestine" title="Peasants&#39; revolt in Palestine">revolt by Palestinian Arab peasants</a> broke out against Egyptian conscription and taxation policies under <a href="/wiki/Muhammad_Ali_of_Egypt" class="mw-redirect" title="Muhammad Ali of Egypt">Muhammad Ali</a>. Although the revolt was suppressed, Muhammad Ali's army retreated and Ottoman rule was restored with British support in 1840.<sup id="cite_ref-121" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-121">&#91;115&#93;</a></sup> Shortly after, the <a href="/wiki/Tanzimat" title="Tanzimat">Tanzimat</a> reforms were implemented across the Ottoman Empire.
</p><p>Since the existence of the earliest <a href="/wiki/Jewish_diaspora" title="Jewish diaspora">Jewish diaspora</a>, many Jews have aspired to <a href="/wiki/Aliyah" title="Aliyah">return</a> to "Zion" and the "Land of Israel",<sup id="cite_ref-122" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-122">&#91;116&#93;</a></sup> though the amount of effort that should be spent towards such an aim was a matter of dispute.<sup id="cite_ref-123" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-123">&#91;117&#93;</a></sup> During the 16th century, Jewish communities struck roots in the <a href="/wiki/Four_Holy_Cities" title="Four Holy Cities">Four Holy Cities</a>—<a href="/wiki/Jerusalem" title="Jerusalem">Jerusalem</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tiberias" title="Tiberias">Tiberias</a>, <a href="/wiki/Hebron" title="Hebron">Hebron</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Safed" title="Safed">Safed</a>—and in 1697, Rabbi Yehuda Hachasid led a group of 1,500 Jews to Jerusalem.<sup id="cite_ref-124" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-124">&#91;118&#93;</a></sup> In the second half of the 18th century, Eastern European <a href="/wiki/Misnagdim" title="Misnagdim">opponents</a> of <a href="/wiki/Hasidic_Judaism" title="Hasidic Judaism">Hasidism</a>, known as the <a href="/wiki/Perushim" title="Perushim">Perushim</a>, settled in Palestine.<sup id="cite_ref-125" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-125">&#91;119&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-126" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-126">&#91;120&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
