style="display:flex"><div class="thumbcaption"><a href="/wiki/Satellite_imagery" title="Satellite imagery">Satellite images</a> of Israel and neighboring territories during the day and night</div></div></div></div>
<p>Israel is located in the <a href="/wiki/Levant" title="Levant">Levant</a> area of the <a href="/wiki/Fertile_Crescent" title="Fertile Crescent">Fertile Crescent</a> region. The country is at the <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Mediterranean" title="Eastern Mediterranean">eastern end</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Mediterranean_Sea" title="Mediterranean Sea">Mediterranean Sea</a>, bounded by Lebanon to the north, Syria to the northeast, Jordan and the West Bank to the east, and Egypt and the Gaza Strip to the southwest. It lies between latitudes <a href="/wiki/29th_parallel_north" title="29th parallel north">29°</a> and <a href="/wiki/34th_parallel_north" title="34th parallel north">34° N</a>, and longitudes <a href="/wiki/34th_meridian_east" title="34th meridian east">34°</a> and <a href="/wiki/36th_meridian_east" title="36th meridian east">36° E</a>.
</p><p>The sovereign territory of Israel (according to the demarcation lines of the <a href="/wiki/1949_Armistice_Agreements" title="1949 Armistice Agreements">1949 Armistice Agreements</a> and excluding all territories captured by Israel during the 1967 <a href="/wiki/Six-Day_War" title="Six-Day War">Six-Day War</a>) is approximately 20,770 square kilometers (8,019&#160;sq&#160;mi) in area, of which two&#160;percent is water.<sup id="cite_ref-cia_280-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cia-280">&#91;273&#93;</a></sup> However Israel is so narrow (100&#160;km at its widest, compared to 400&#160;km from north to south) that the <a href="/wiki/Exclusive_economic_zone" title="Exclusive economic zone">exclusive economic zone</a> in the Mediterranean is double the land area of the country.<sup id="cite_ref-281" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-281">&#91;274&#93;</a></sup> The total area under Israeli law, including <a href="/wiki/East_Jerusalem" title="East Jerusalem">East Jerusalem</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Golan_Heights" title="Golan Heights">Golan Heights</a>, is 22,072 square kilometers (8,522&#160;sq&#160;mi),<sup id="cite_ref-282" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-282">&#91;275&#93;</a></sup> and the total area under Israeli control, including the military-controlled and partially <a href="/wiki/Palestinian_National_Authority" title="Palestinian National Authority">Palestinian-governed</a> territory of the <a href="/wiki/West_Bank" title="West Bank">West Bank</a>, is 27,799 square kilometers (10,733&#160;sq&#160;mi).<sup id="cite_ref-loc-geo_283-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-loc-geo-283">&#91;276&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Despite its small size, Israel is home to a variety of geographic features, from the <a href="/wiki/Negev" title="Negev">Negev</a> desert in the south to the inland fertile <a href="/wiki/Jezreel_Valley" title="Jezreel Valley">Jezreel Valley</a>, mountain ranges of the <a href="/wiki/Galilee" title="Galilee">Galilee</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mount_Carmel" title="Mount Carmel">Carmel</a> and toward the <a href="/wiki/Golan_Heights" title="Golan Heights">Golan</a> in the north. The <a href="/wiki/Israeli_coastal_plain" title="Israeli coastal plain">Israeli coastal plain</a> on the shores of the Mediterranean is home to most of the nation's population.<sup id="cite_ref-284" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-284">&#91;277&#93;</a></sup> East of the central highlands lies the <a href="/wiki/Jordan_Rift_Valley" title="Jordan Rift Valley">Jordan Rift Valley</a>, which forms a small part of the 6,500-kilometer (4,039&#160;mi) <a href="/wiki/Great_Rift_Valley" title="Great Rift Valley">Great Rift Valley</a>. The <a href="/wiki/Jordan_River" title="Jordan River">Jordan River</a> runs along the Jordan Rift Valley, from <a href="/wiki/Mount_Hermon" title="Mount Hermon">Mount Hermon</a> through the <a href="/wiki/Hulah_Valley" class="mw-redirect" title="Hulah Valley">Hulah Valley</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Sea_of_Galilee" title="Sea of Galilee">Sea of Galilee</a> to the <a href="/wiki/Dead_Sea" title="Dead Sea">Dead Sea</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Extreme_points_of_Earth" class="mw-redirect" title="Extreme points of Earth">lowest point</a> on the surface of the Earth.<sup id="cite_ref-285" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-285">&#91;278&#93;</a></sup> Further south is the <a href="/wiki/Arabah" title="Arabah">Arabah</a>, ending with the <a href="/wiki/Gulf_of_Aqaba" title="Gulf of Aqaba">Gulf of Eilat</a>, part of the <a href="/wiki/Red_Sea" title="Red Sea">Red Sea</a>. <a href="/wiki/Makhtesh" title="Makhtesh">Makhtesh</a>, or "erosion cirques" are unique to the <a href="/wiki/Negev" title="Negev">Negev</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Sinai_Peninsula" title="Sinai Peninsula">Sinai Peninsula</a>, the largest being the <a href="/wiki/Makhtesh_Ramon" title="Makhtesh Ramon">Makhtesh Ramon</a> at 38&#160;km in length.<sup id="cite_ref-286" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-286">&#91;279&#93;</a></sup> A report on the environmental status of the <a href="/wiki/Mediterranean_Basin" title="Mediterranean Basin">Mediterranean Basin</a> states that Israel has the largest number of plant species per square meter of all the countries in the basin.<sup id="cite_ref-rinat_287-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-rinat-287">&#91;280&#93;</a></sup> Israel contains four terrestrial ecoregions: <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Mediterranean_conifer-sclerophyllous-broadleaf_forests" class="mw-redirect" title="Eastern Mediterranean conifer-sclerophyllous-broadleaf forests">Eastern Mediterranean conifer-sclerophyllous-broadleaf forests</a>, <a href="/wiki/Southern_Anatolian_montane_conifer_and_deciduous_forests" title="Southern Anatolian montane conifer and deciduous forests">Southern Anatolian montane conifer and deciduous forests</a>, <a href="/wiki/Arabian_Desert" title="Arabian Desert">Arabian Desert</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Mesopotamian_shrub_desert" title="Mesopotamian shrub desert">Mesopotamian shrub desert</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-DinersteinOlson2017_288-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-DinersteinOlson2017-288">&#91;281&#93;</a></sup> It had a 2019 <a href="/wiki/Forest_Landscape_Integrity_Index" title="Forest Landscape Integrity Index">Forest Landscape Integrity Index</a> mean score of 4.14/10, ranking it 135th globally out of 172 countries.<sup id="cite_ref-FLII-Supplementary_289-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FLII-Supplementary-289">&#91;282&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Tectonics_and_seismicity">Tectonics and seismicity</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/List_of_earthquakes_in_the_Levant" title="List of earthquakes in the Levant">List of earthquakes in the Levant</a></div>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/Jordan_Rift_Valley" title="Jordan Rift Valley">Jordan Rift Valley</a> is the result of tectonic movements within the <a href="/wiki/Dead_Sea_Transform" title="Dead Sea Transform">Dead Sea Transform</a> (DSF) fault system. The DSF forms the <a href="/wiki/Transform_fault" title="Transform fault">transform boundary</a> between the <a href="/wiki/African_Plate" title="African Plate">African Plate</a> to the west and the <a href="/wiki/Arabian_Plate" title="Arabian Plate">Arabian Plate</a> to the east. The Golan Heights and all of <a href="/wiki/Jordan" title="Jordan">Jordan</a> are part of the Arabian Plate, while the Galilee, West Bank, Coastal Plain, and Negev along with the Sinai Peninsula are on the African Plate. This tectonic disposition leads to a relatively high <a href="/wiki/List_of_earthquakes_in_the_Levant" title="List of earthquakes in the Levant">seismic activity in the region</a>. The entire Jordan Valley segment is thought to have ruptured repeatedly, for instance during the last two major <a href="/wiki/Geography_of_Israel#Seismic_activity" title="Geography of Israel">earthquakes</a> along this structure in <a href="/wiki/749_Galilee_earthquake" title="749 Galilee earthquake">749</a> and <a href="/wiki/1033_Jordan_Rift_Valley_earthquake" title="1033 Jordan Rift Valley earthquake">1033</a>. The deficit in <a href="/wiki/Fault_(geology)#Slip,_heave,_throw" title="Fault (geology)">slip</a> that has built up since the 1033 event is sufficient to cause an earthquake of M<sub>w</sub>&#8239;~7.4.<sup id="cite_ref-Ferry_290-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ferry-290">&#91;283&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The most catastrophic known earthquakes occurred in 31 BCE, <a href="/wiki/Galilee_earthquake_of_363" class="mw-redirect" title="Galilee earthquake of 363">363</a>, 749, and 1033 CE, that is every <abbr title="circa">ca.</abbr> 400 years on average.<sup id="cite_ref-MarcoAFTAU_291-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-MarcoAFTAU-291">&#91;284&#93;</a></sup> Destructive earthquakes leading to serious loss of life strike about every 80 years.<sup id="cite_ref-IllPreped_292-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-IllPreped-292">&#91;285&#93;</a></sup> While stringent construction regulations are currently in place and recently built structures are earthquake-safe, as of 2007<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Israel&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup> the majority of the buildings in Israel were older than these regulations and many public buildings as well as 50,000 residential buildings did not meet the new standards and were "expected to collapse" if exposed to a strong earthquake.<sup id="cite_ref-IllPreped_292-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-IllPreped-292">&#91;285&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Climate">Climate</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Climate_change_in_Israel" title="Climate change in Israel">Climate change in Israel</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Koppen-Geiger_Map_ISR_present.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ea/Koppen-Geiger_Map_ISR_present.svg/260px-Koppen-Geiger_Map_ISR_present.svg.png" decoding="async" width="260" height="197" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ea/Koppen-Geiger_Map_ISR_present.svg/390px-Koppen-Geiger_Map_ISR_present.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ea/Koppen-Geiger_Map_ISR_present.svg/520px-Koppen-Geiger_Map_ISR_present.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="1124" data-file-height="850" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification" title="Köppen climate classification">Köppen climate classification</a> map of Israel and the <a href="/wiki/Golan_Heights" title="Golan Heights">Golan Heights</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>Temperatures in Israel vary widely, especially during the winter. Coastal areas, such as those of <a href="/wiki/Tel_Aviv" title="Tel Aviv">Tel Aviv</a> and <a href="/wiki/Haifa" title="Haifa">Haifa</a>, have a typical <a href="/wiki/Mediterranean_climate" title="Mediterranean climate">Mediterranean climate</a> with cool, rainy winters and long, hot summers. The area of <a href="/wiki/Beersheba" title="Beersheba">Beersheba</a> and the Northern Negev have a <a href="/wiki/Semi-arid_climate" title="Semi-arid climate">semi-arid climate</a> with hot summers, cool winters, and fewer rainy days than the Mediterranean climate. The Southern Negev and the Arava areas have a <a href="/wiki/Desert_climate" title="Desert climate">desert climate</a> with very hot, dry summers, and mild winters with few days of rain. The highest temperature in the world outside Africa and North America as of 2021<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Israel&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup>, 54&#160;°C (129&#160;°F), was recorded in 1942 in the <a href="/wiki/Tirat_Zvi" title="Tirat Zvi">Tirat Zvi</a> kibbutz in the northern Jordan River valley.<sup id="cite_ref-watzman_293-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-watzman-293">&#91;286&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-294" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-294">&#91;287&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>At the other extreme, mountainous regions can be windy and cold, and areas at elevation of 750 metres (2,460&#160;ft) or more (same elevation as Jerusalem) will usually receive at least one <a href="/wiki/Snow_in_Israel" title="Snow in Israel">snowfall</a> each year.<sup id="cite_ref-295" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-295">&#91;288&#93;</a></sup> From May to September, rain in Israel is rare.<sup id="cite_ref-296" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-296">&#91;289&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-297" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-297">&#91;290&#93;</a></sup> With scarce water resources, Israel has developed various water-saving technologies, including <a href="/wiki/Drip_irrigation" title="Drip irrigation">drip irrigation</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-298" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-298">&#91;291&#93;</a></sup><sup class="noprint Inline-Template noprint noexcerpt Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:NOTRS" class="mw-redirect" title="Wikipedia:NOTRS"><span title="This claim needs references to better sources. (January 2023)">better&#160;source&#160;needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup> Israelis also take advantage of the considerable sunlight available for <a href="/wiki/Solar_energy" title="Solar energy">solar energy</a>, making <a href="/wiki/Solar_power_in_Israel" title="Solar power in Israel">Israel the leading nation in solar energy</a> use per capita—practically every house uses solar panels for water heating.<sup id="cite_ref-Solar_energy_299-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Solar_energy-299">&#91;292&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Soil_moisture_and_climate_change.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8d/Soil_moisture_and_climate_change.svg/260px-Soil_moisture_and_climate_change.svg.png" decoding="async" width="260" height="204" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8d/Soil_moisture_and_climate_change.svg/390px-Soil_moisture_and_climate_change.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8d/Soil_moisture_and_climate_change.svg/520px-Soil_moisture_and_climate_change.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="960" data-file-height="755" /></a><figcaption>The projections of the <a href="/wiki/IPCC_Sixth_Assessment_Report" title="IPCC Sixth Assessment Report">IPCC Sixth Assessment Report</a> show clearly the impacts of climate change on Israel even at 2 degrees of warming.</figcaption></figure>
<p>There are four different <a href="/wiki/Phytogeographic" class="mw-redirect" title="Phytogeographic">phytogeographic</a> regions in Israel, due to the country's location between the temperate and tropical zones, bordering the Mediterranean Sea in the west and the desert in the east. For this reason, the flora and fauna of Israel are extremely diverse. There are 2,867 known <a href="/wiki/List_of_endemic_flora_of_Israel" title="List of endemic flora of Israel">species of plants found in Israel</a>. Of these, at least 253 species are <a href="/wiki/List_of_adventive_wild_plants_in_Israel" title="List of adventive wild plants in Israel">introduced</a> and non-native.<sup id="cite_ref-300" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-300">&#91;293&#93;</a></sup> There are 380 <a href="/wiki/National_parks_and_nature_reserves_of_Israel" title="National parks and nature reserves of Israel">Israeli nature reserves</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-301" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-301">&#91;294&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The Israeli <a href="/wiki/Ministry_of_Environmental_Protection_(Israel)" title="Ministry of Environmental Protection (Israel)">Ministry of Environmental Protection</a> has reported that <a href="/wiki/Climate_change_in_Israel" title="Climate change in Israel">climate change</a> "will have a decisive impact on all areas of life, including: water, public health, agriculture, energy, biodiversity, coastal infrastructure, economics, nature, national security, and geostrategy", and will have the greatest effect on vulnerable populations such as the poor, the elderly, and the chronically ill.<sup id="cite_ref-MEP_2020_302-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-MEP_2020-302">&#91;295&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Demographics">Demographics</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Demographics_of_Israel" title="Demographics of Israel">Demographics of Israel</a> and <a href="/wiki/Israelis" title="Israelis">Israelis</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Israelpop.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/Israelpop.svg/220px-Israelpop.svg.png" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/Israelpop.svg/330px-Israelpop.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/Israelpop.svg/440px-Israelpop.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="800" data-file-height="600" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Population_pyramid" title="Population pyramid">Population pyramid</a> of Israel</figcaption></figure>
<p>As of 31&#160;December&#160;2022<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Israel&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup>, Israel's population was an estimated 9,656,000. In 2022, the civil government recorded 73.6% of the population as <a href="/wiki/Israeli_Jews" title="Israeli Jews">Jews</a>, 21.1% of the population as <a href="/wiki/Arab_citizens_of_Israel" title="Arab citizens of Israel">Arabs</a>, and 5.3% as "Others" (non-Arab Christians and people who have no religion listed).<sup id="cite_ref-population_stat2022_14-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-population_stat2022-14">&#91;11&#93;</a></sup> Over the last decade, large numbers of migrant workers from Romania, Thailand, China, Africa, and South America have settled in Israel. Exact figures are unknown, as many of them are living in the country illegally,<sup id="cite_ref-303" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-303">&#91;296&#93;</a></sup> but estimates run from 166,000 to 203,000.<sup id="cite_ref-Adriana_Kemp_304-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Adriana_Kemp-304">&#91;297&#93;</a></sup> By June 2012, approximately 60,000 <a href="/wiki/Illegal_immigration_from_Africa_to_Israel" class="mw-redirect" title="Illegal immigration from Africa to Israel">African migrants</a> had entered Israel.<sup id="cite_ref-305" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-305">&#91;298&#93;</a></sup> About 93% of Israelis live in urban areas.<sup id="cite_ref-306" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-306">&#91;299&#93;</a></sup> 90% of <a href="/wiki/Palestinian_citizens_of_Israel" title="Palestinian citizens of Israel">Palestinian Israelis</a> reside in 139 densely populated towns and villages concentrated in the Galilee, <a href="/wiki/Triangle_(Israel)" title="Triangle (Israel)">Triangle</a> and <a href="/wiki/Negev" title="Negev">Negev</a> regions, with the remaining 10% in <a href="/wiki/Mixed_cities" title="Mixed cities">mixed cities</a> and neighbourhoods.<sup id="cite_ref-307" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-307">&#91;300&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-308" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-308">&#91;301&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-309" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-309">&#91;302&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-310" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-310">&#91;303&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-311" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-311">&#91;304&#93;</a></sup> Data published by the <a href="/wiki/Organisation_for_Economic_Co-operation_and_Development" class="mw-redirect" title="Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development">OECD</a> in 2016 estimated the average <a href="/wiki/Life_expectancy" title="Life expectancy">life expectancy</a> of Israelis at 82.5 years, making it the <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_life_expectancy" title="List of countries by life expectancy">6th-highest in the world</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-OECD_life_expec_312-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-OECD_life_expec-312">&#91;305&#93;</a></sup> Israeli Arab life expectancy lags behind by 3 to 4 years,<sup id="cite_ref-313" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-313">&#91;306&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-314" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-314">&#91;307&#93;</a></sup> still higher than almost every majority Arab or Muslim country in the world.<sup id="cite_ref-315" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-315">&#91;308&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-316" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-316">&#91;309&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Aliyah_1948-2015.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ce/Aliyah_1948-2015.png/300px-Aliyah_1948-2015.png" decoding="async" width="300" height="119" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ce/Aliyah_1948-2015.png/450px-Aliyah_1948-2015.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ce/Aliyah_1948-2015.png/600px-Aliyah_1948-2015.png 2x" data-file-width="1617" data-file-height="642" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Immigration_to_Israel" class="mw-redirect" title="Immigration to Israel">Immigration to Israel</a> in the years 1948–2015. The two peaks were in 1949 and 1990.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Israel was established as a <a href="/wiki/Homeland_for_the_Jewish_people" title="Homeland for the Jewish people">homeland for the Jewish people</a> and is often referred to as a <a href="/wiki/Jewish_state" title="Jewish state">Jewish state</a>. The country's <a href="/wiki/Law_of_Return" title="Law of Return">Law of Return</a> grants all Jews and those of Jewish ancestry the right to <a href="/wiki/Israeli_nationality_law" class="mw-redirect" title="Israeli nationality law">Israeli citizenship</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-317" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-317">&#91;310&#93;</a></sup> Retention of Israel's population since 1948 is about even or greater, when compared to other countries with mass immigration.<sup id="cite_ref-318" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-318">&#91;311&#93;</a></sup> Jewish emigration from Israel (called <i><a href="/wiki/Yerida" title="Yerida">yerida</a></i> in Hebrew), primarily to the United States and Canada, is described by demographers as modest,<sup id="cite_ref-319" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-319">&#91;312&#93;</a></sup> but is often cited by Israeli government ministries as a major threat to Israel's future.<sup id="cite_ref-320" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-320">&#91;313&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-321" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-321">&#91;314&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Approximately 80% of <a href="/wiki/Israeli_Jews" title="Israeli Jews">Israeli Jews</a> are <a href="/wiki/Sabra_(person)" title="Sabra (person)">born in Israel</a>, 14% are immigrants from Europe and the Americas, and 6% are immigrants from Asia and Africa.<sup id="cite_ref-322" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-322">&#91;315&#93;</a></sup> Jews from Europe and the former <a href="/wiki/Soviet_Union" title="Soviet Union">Soviet Union</a> and their descendants born in Israel, including <a href="/wiki/Ashkenazi_Jews" title="Ashkenazi Jews">Ashkenazi Jews</a>, constitute approximately 50% of Jewish Israelis. <a href="/wiki/Jewish_exodus_from_Arab_and_Muslim_countries" class="mw-redirect" title="Jewish exodus from Arab and Muslim countries">Jews who left or fled Arab and Muslim countries</a> and their descendants, including both <a href="/wiki/Mizrahi_Jews" title="Mizrahi Jews">Mizrahi</a> and <a href="/wiki/Sephardi_Jews" class="mw-redirect" title="Sephardi Jews">Sephardi</a> Jews,<sup id="cite_ref-323" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-323">&#91;316&#93;</a></sup> form most of the rest of the Jewish population.<sup id="cite_ref-324" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-324">&#91;317&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-325" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-325">&#91;318&#93;</a></sup> Jewish intermarriage rates run at over 35% and recent studies suggest that the percentage of Israelis descended from both Sephardi and Ashkenazi Jews increases by 0.5 percent every year, with over 25% of school children now originating from both communities.<sup id="cite_ref-326" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-326">&#91;319&#93;</a></sup> Around 4% of Israelis (300,000), ethnically defined as "others", are <a href="/wiki/1990s_Post-Soviet_aliyah" class="mw-redirect" title="1990s Post-Soviet aliyah">Russian descendants</a> of Jewish origin or family who are not Jewish according to rabbinical law, but were eligible for Israeli citizenship under the Law of Return.<sup id="cite_ref-DellaPergola,_Sergio_2011_327-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-DellaPergola,_Sergio_2011-327">&#91;320&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Israel_people_328-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Israel_people-328">&#91;321&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-329" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-329">&#91;322&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The total number of <a href="/wiki/Israeli_settlement" title="Israeli settlement">Israeli settlers</a> beyond the <a href="/wiki/Green_Line_(Israel)" title="Green Line (Israel)">Green Line</a> is over 600,000 (≈10% of the Jewish Israeli population).<sup id="cite_ref-330" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-330">&#91;323&#93;</a></sup> In 2016<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Israel&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup>, 399,300 Israelis <a href="/wiki/Population_statistics_for_Israeli_settlements_in_the_West_Bank" title="Population statistics for Israeli settlements in the West Bank">lived</a> in <a href="/wiki/West_Bank" title="West Bank">West Bank</a> settlements,<sup id="cite_ref-districts_pop_331-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-districts_pop-331">&#91;324&#93;</a></sup> including those that predated the establishment of the State of Israel and which were re-established after the <a href="/wiki/Six-Day_War" title="Six-Day War">Six-Day War</a>, in cities such as <a href="/wiki/Hebron" title="Hebron">Hebron</a> and <a href="/wiki/Gush_Etzion" title="Gush Etzion">Gush Etzion</a> bloc. In addition to the West Bank settlements, there were more than 200,000 Jews living in <a href="/wiki/East_Jerusalem" title="East Jerusalem">East Jerusalem</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-jerusalem_pop_332-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-jerusalem_pop-332">&#91;325&#93;</a></sup> and 22,000 in the <a href="/wiki/Golan_Heights" title="Golan Heights">Golan Heights</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-districts_pop_331-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-districts_pop-331">&#91;324&#93;</a></sup> Approximately 7,800 Israelis <a href="/wiki/Population_statistics_for_Israeli_Gaza_Strip_settlements" class="mw-redirect" title="Population statistics for Israeli Gaza Strip settlements">lived in settlements</a> in the Gaza Strip, known as <a href="/wiki/Gush_Katif" title="Gush Katif">Gush Katif</a>, until they were evacuated by the government as part of its 2005 <a href="/wiki/Israel%27s_unilateral_disengagement_plan" class="mw-redirect" title="Israel&#39;s unilateral disengagement plan">disengagement plan</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-333" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-333">&#91;326&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Israeli Arabs (including the Arab population of East Jerusalem and the Golan Heights) comprise 21.1% of the population or 1,995,000 people.<sup id="cite_ref-334" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-334">&#91;327&#93;</a></sup> In a 2017 telephone poll, 40% of Arab citizens of Israel identified as "Arab in Israel" or "Arab citizen of Israel", 15% identified as "Palestinian", 8.9% as "Palestinian in Israel" or "Palestinian citizen of Israel", and 8.7% as "Arab"; 60% of Israeli Arabs have a positive view of the state.<sup id="cite_ref-335" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-335">&#91;328&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-336" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-336">&#91;329&#93;</a></sup> According to <a href="/wiki/Sammy_Smooha" title="Sammy Smooha">Sammy Smooha</a>, "The identity of 83.0% of the Arabs in 2019 (up from 75.5% in 2017) has an Israeli component and 61.9% (unchanged from 60.3%) has a Palestinian component. However, when these two components were presented as competitors, 69.0% of the Arabs in 2019 chose exclusive or primary Palestinian identity, compared with 29.8% who chose exclusive or primary Israeli Arab identity."<sup id="cite_ref-337" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-337">&#91;330&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Major_urban_areas">Major urban areas</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">For a more comprehensive list, see <a href="/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Israel" title="List of cities in Israel">List of cities in Israel</a>.</div>
<div class="thumb tnone" style="margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;overflow:hidden;width:auto;max-width:908px"><div class="thumbinner"><div class="noresize" style="overflow:auto"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:Tel_Aviv_Panorama.jpg" class="mw-file-description" title="View over the Tel Aviv Metropolitan Area"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/93/Tel_Aviv_Panorama.jpg/900px-Tel_Aviv_Panorama.jpg" decoding="async" width="900" height="183" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/93/Tel_Aviv_Panorama.jpg/1350px-Tel_Aviv_Panorama.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/93/Tel_Aviv_Panorama.jpg/1800px-Tel_Aviv_Panorama.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4863" data-file-height="987" /></a></span></div><div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Tel_Aviv_Panorama.jpg" title="File:Tel Aviv Panorama.jpg"> </a></div>View over the <a href="/wiki/Tel_Aviv_Metropolitan_Area" class="mw-redirect" title="Tel Aviv Metropolitan Area">Tel Aviv Metropolitan Area</a></div></div></div>
<p>Israel has four major metropolitan areas: <a href="/wiki/Gush_Dan" title="Gush Dan">Gush Dan</a> (Tel Aviv metropolitan area; population 3,854,000), <a href="/wiki/Jerusalem_metropolitan_area" class="mw-redirect" title="Jerusalem metropolitan area">Jerusalem metropolitan area</a> (population 1,253,900), <a href="/wiki/Haifa_metropolitan_area" title="Haifa metropolitan area">Haifa metropolitan area</a> (population 924,400), and <a href="/wiki/Beersheba_metropolitan_area" title="Beersheba metropolitan area">Beersheba metropolitan area</a> (population 377,100).<sup id="cite_ref-338" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-338">&#91;331&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Israel's largest municipality, in population and area, is <a href="/wiki/Jerusalem" title="Jerusalem">Jerusalem</a> with 966,210 residents in an area of 125 square kilometres (48&#160;sq&#160;mi).<sup id="cite_ref-Israelpopulations_339-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Israelpopulations-339">&#91;332&#93;</a></sup> Israeli government statistics on Jerusalem include the population and area of <a href="/wiki/East_Jerusalem" title="East Jerusalem">East Jerusalem</a>, which is widely recognized as part of the <a href="/wiki/Palestinian_territories" title="Palestinian territories">Palestinian territories</a> under <a href="/wiki/Israeli-occupied_territories" title="Israeli-occupied territories">Israeli occupation</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-340" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-340">&#91;333&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Tel_Aviv" title="Tel Aviv">Tel Aviv</a> and <a href="/wiki/Haifa" title="Haifa">Haifa</a> rank as Israel's next most populous cities, with populations of 467,875 and 282,832, respectively.<sup id="cite_ref-Israelpopulations_339-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Israelpopulations-339">&#91;332&#93;</a></sup>
The (mainly <a href="/wiki/Haredi" class="mw-redirect" title="Haredi">Haredi</a>) city of <a href="/wiki/Bnei_Brak" title="Bnei Brak">Bnei Brak</a> is the most densely populated city in Israel and one of the <a href="/wiki/List_of_cities_proper_by_population_density" title="List of cities proper by population density">10 most densely populated cities</a> in the world.<sup id="cite_ref-341" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-341">&#91;334&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Israel has 16 <a href="/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Israel" title="List of cities in Israel">cities</a> with populations over 100,000. In all, there are 77 Israeli localities granted <a href="/wiki/City_council_(Israel)" title="City council (Israel)">"municipalities" (or "city") status</a> by the Ministry of the Interior,<sup id="cite_ref-342" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-342">&#91;335&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/List_of_Israeli_settlements_with_city_status_in_the_West_Bank" class="mw-redirect" title="List of Israeli settlements with city status in the West Bank">four of which are in the West Bank</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-343" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-343">&#91;336&#93;</a></sup> Two more cities are planned: <a href="/wiki/Kasif,_Israel" title="Kasif, Israel">Kasif</a>, a <a href="/wiki/Planned_city" class="mw-redirect" title="Planned city">planned city</a> to be built in the <a href="/wiki/Negev" title="Negev">Negev</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Harish,_Israel" title="Harish, Israel">Harish</a>, originally a small town that is being built into a large city since 2015.<sup id="cite_ref-344" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-344">&#91;337&#93;</a></sup>
</p>

</p><h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Language">Language</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Languages_of_Israel" title="Languages of Israel">Languages of Israel</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:%D7%A9%D7%9C%D7%98_%D7%A8%D7%97%D7%95%D7%91_%D7%99%D7%94%D7%95%D7%93%D7%94_(3777232251).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/28/%D7%A9%D7%9C%D7%98_%D7%A8%D7%97%D7%95%D7%91_%D7%99%D7%94%D7%95%D7%93%D7%94_%283777232251%29.jpg/220px-%D7%A9%D7%9C%D7%98_%D7%A8%D7%97%D7%95%D7%91_%D7%99%D7%94%D7%95%D7%93%D7%94_%283777232251%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/28/%D7%A9%D7%9C%D7%98_%D7%A8%D7%97%D7%95%D7%91_%D7%99%D7%94%D7%95%D7%93%D7%94_%283777232251%29.jpg/330px-%D7%A9%D7%9C%D7%98_%D7%A8%D7%97%D7%95%D7%91_%D7%99%D7%94%D7%95%D7%93%D7%94_%283777232251%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/28/%D7%A9%D7%9C%D7%98_%D7%A8%D7%97%D7%95%D7%91_%D7%99%D7%94%D7%95%D7%93%D7%94_%283777232251%29.jpg/440px-%D7%A9%D7%9C%D7%98_%D7%A8%D7%97%D7%95%D7%91_%D7%99%D7%94%D7%95%D7%93%D7%94_%283777232251%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2560" data-file-height="1920" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Road_signs_in_Israel" title="Road signs in Israel">Road sign</a> in <a href="/wiki/Hebrew_language" title="Hebrew language">Hebrew</a>, Arabic, and English</figcaption></figure>
<p>Israel's sole official language is <a href="/wiki/Hebrew_language" title="Hebrew language">Hebrew</a>. Until 2018, <a href="/wiki/Arabic_language_in_Israel" title="Arabic language in Israel">Arabic</a> was also one of two official languages of the State of Israel;<sup id="cite_ref-lang1_10-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-lang1-10">&#91;8&#93;</a></sup> in 2018 <a href="/wiki/Basic_Law:_Israel_as_the_Nation-State_of_the_Jewish_People" title="Basic Law: Israel as the Nation-State of the Jewish People">it was downgraded</a> to having a 'special status in the state' with its use by state institutions to be set in law.<sup id="cite_ref-lang2_11-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-lang2-11">&#91;9&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-lang3_12-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-lang3-12">&#91;10&#93;</a></sup> Hebrew is the primary language of the state and is spoken every day by the majority of the population. Arabic is spoken by the Arab minority, with Hebrew taught in Arab schools.
</p><p>As a country of <a href="/wiki/Aliyah" title="Aliyah">immigrants</a>, many languages can be heard on the streets. Due to mass immigration from the former Soviet Union and <a href="/wiki/Aliyah_from_Ethiopia" title="Aliyah from Ethiopia">Ethiopia</a> (some 130,000 <a href="/wiki/Ethiopian_Jews_in_Israel" title="Ethiopian Jews in Israel">Ethiopian Jews live in Israel</a>),<sup id="cite_ref-The_Ethiopian_Population_In_Israel_346-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-The_Ethiopian_Population_In_Israel-346">&#91;339&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-347" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-347">&#91;340&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Russian_language_in_Israel" title="Russian language in Israel">Russian</a> and <a href="/wiki/Amharic" title="Amharic">Amharic</a> are widely spoken.<sup id="cite_ref-348" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-348">&#91;341&#93;</a></sup> More than one million Russian-speaking immigrants <a href="/wiki/1990s_Post-Soviet_aliyah" class="mw-redirect" title="1990s Post-Soviet aliyah">arrived</a> in Israel from the post-Soviet states between 1990 and 2004.<sup id="cite_ref-349" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-349">&#91;342&#93;</a></sup> French is spoken by around 700,000 Israelis,<sup id="cite_ref-350" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-350">&#91;343&#93;</a></sup> mostly originating <a href="/wiki/French_Jews_in_Israel" title="French Jews in Israel">from France</a> and North Africa (see <a href="/wiki/Maghrebi_Jews" title="Maghrebi Jews">Maghrebi Jews</a>). English was an official language during the Mandate period; it lost this status after the establishment of Israel, but retains a role comparable to that of an official language,<sup id="cite_ref-351" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-351">&#91;344&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-352" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-352">&#91;345&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-353" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-353">&#91;346&#93;</a></sup> as may be seen in <a href="/wiki/Road_signs_in_Israel" title="Road signs in Israel">road signs</a> and official documents. Many Israelis communicate reasonably well in English, as many television programmes are broadcast in English with <a href="/wiki/Subtitles" title="Subtitles">subtitles</a> and the language is taught from the early grades in elementary school. In addition, Israeli universities offer courses in the English language on various subjects.<sup id="cite_ref-354" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-354">&#91;347&#93;</a></sup><sup class="noprint Inline-Template noprint noexcerpt Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:NOTRS" class="mw-redirect" title="Wikipedia:NOTRS"><span title="This claim needs references to better sources. (January 2023)">better&#160;source&#160;needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup>
</p>

<div class="center" style="width:auto; margin-left:auto; margin-right:auto;"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1097763485"><table class="box-Notice plainlinks metadata ambox ambox-notice" role="presentation" style="width:100%;margin:0;"><tbody><tr><td class="mbox-image"><div class="mbox-image-div"><span typeof="mw:File"><span><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/1/1d/Information_icon4.svg/40px-Information_icon4.svg.png" decoding="async" width="40" height="40" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/1/1d/Information_icon4.svg/60px-Information_icon4.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/1/1d/Information_icon4.svg/80px-Information_icon4.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="620" data-file-height="620" /></span></span></div></td><td class="mbox-text" style="text-align: left;"><div class="mbox-text-span">Graphs are temporarily unavailable due to technical issues.</div></td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<div class="center" style="width:auto; margin-left:auto; margin-right:auto;"><span style="margin:0px; font-size:90%;"><span style="border:none; background-color:navy; color:navy;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Israeli_Jews" title="Israeli Jews">Jewish</a></span>, <span style="margin:0px; font-size:90%;"><span style="border:none; background-color:green; color:green;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Islam_in_Israel" title="Islam in Israel">Muslim</a></span>, <span style="margin:0px; font-size:90%;"><span style="border:none; background-color:red; color:red;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Christianity_in_Israel" title="Christianity in Israel">Christian</a></span>, <span style="margin:0px; font-size:90%;"><span style="border:none; background-color:black; color:black;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Druze_in_Israel" title="Druze in Israel">Druze</a></span>, <span style="margin:0px; font-size:90%;"><span style="border:none; background-color:gray; color:gray;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Religion_in_Israel" title="Religion in Israel">Other</a></span>.<br />
Until 1995, figures for Christians also included Others.<sup id="cite_ref-355" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-355">&#91;348&#93;</a></sup></div>
</div></div>
<p>Israel comprises a major part of the <a href="/wiki/Holy_Land" title="Holy Land">Holy Land</a>, a region of significant importance to all <a href="/wiki/Abrahamic_religions" title="Abrahamic religions">Abrahamic religions</a>, including <a href="/wiki/Judaism" title="Judaism">Judaism</a>, <a href="/wiki/Christianity" title="Christianity">Christianity</a>, <a href="/wiki/Islam" title="Islam">Islam</a>, <a href="/wiki/Samaritanism" title="Samaritanism">Samaritanism</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Druze" title="Druze">Druze Faith</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Bah%C3%A1%CA%BC%C3%AD_Faith" title="Baháʼí Faith">Baháʼí Faith</a>.
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Jewish_religious_movements" title="Jewish religious movements">religious affiliation</a> of <a href="/wiki/Israeli_Jews" title="Israeli Jews">Israeli Jews</a> varies widely: a social survey from 2016 made by <a href="/wiki/Pew_Research" class="mw-redirect" title="Pew Research">Pew Research</a> indicates that 49% self-identify as <a href="/wiki/Hiloni" title="Hiloni">Hiloni</a> (secular), 29% as <a href="/wiki/Masortim" title="Masortim">Masorti</a> (traditional), 13% as <a href="/wiki/Dati" class="mw-redirect" title="Dati">Dati</a> (religious) and 9% as <a href="/wiki/Haredi_Judaism" title="Haredi Judaism">Haredi</a> (ultra-Orthodox).<sup id="cite_ref-356" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-356">&#91;349&#93;</a></sup> Haredi Jews are expected to represent more than 20% of Israel's Jewish population by 2028.<sup id="cite_ref-357" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-357">&#91;350&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Islam_in_Israel" title="Islam in Israel">Muslims</a> constitute Israel's largest religious minority, making up about 17.6% of the population. About 2% of the population is <a href="/wiki/Christianity_in_Israel" title="Christianity in Israel">Christian</a> and 1.6% is <a href="/wiki/Druze_in_Israel" title="Druze in Israel">Druze</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-cia_280-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cia-280">&#91;273&#93;</a></sup> The Christian population is composed primarily of <a href="/wiki/Arab_Christians" title="Arab Christians">Arab Christians</a> and <a href="/wiki/Arameans_in_Israel" class="mw-redirect" title="Arameans in Israel">Aramean Christians</a>, but also includes post-Soviet immigrants, the foreign laborers of multinational origins, and followers of <a href="/wiki/Messianic_Judaism" title="Messianic Judaism">Messianic Judaism</a>, considered by most Christians and Jews to be a form of Christianity.<sup id="cite_ref-358" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-358">&#91;351&#93;</a></sup> Members of many other religious groups, including <a href="/wiki/Buddhism" title="Buddhism">Buddhists</a> and <a href="/wiki/Hinduism_in_Israel" title="Hinduism in Israel">Hindus</a>, maintain a presence in Israel, albeit in small numbers.<sup id="cite_ref-359" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-359">&#91;352&#93;</a></sup> Out of more than one million <a href="/wiki/1990s_Post-Soviet_aliyah" class="mw-redirect" title="1990s Post-Soviet aliyah">immigrants</a> from the former Soviet Union, about 300,000 are considered not Jewish by the <a href="/wiki/Chief_Rabbinate_of_Israel" title="Chief Rabbinate of Israel">Chief Rabbinate of Israel</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-360" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-360">&#91;353&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Westernwall2.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="A large open area with people bounded by old stone walls. To the left is a mosque with large golden dome." src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/17/Westernwall2.jpg/220px-Westernwall2.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/17/Westernwall2.jpg/330px-Westernwall2.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/17/Westernwall2.jpg/440px-Westernwall2.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2592" data-file-height="1944" /></a><figcaption>The <a href="/wiki/Dome_of_the_Rock" title="Dome of the Rock">Dome of the Rock</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Western_Wall" title="Western Wall">Western Wall</a>, Jerusalem</figcaption></figure>
<p>The city of <a href="/wiki/Jerusalem" title="Jerusalem">Jerusalem</a> is of <a href="/wiki/Religious_significance_of_Jerusalem" title="Religious significance of Jerusalem">special importance</a> to Jews, Muslims, and Christians, as it is the home of <a href="/wiki/List_of_places_in_Jerusalem" title="List of places in Jerusalem">sites</a> that are pivotal to their religious beliefs, such as the <a href="/wiki/Old_City_(Jerusalem)" class="mw-redirect" title="Old City (Jerusalem)">Old City</a> that incorporates the <a href="/wiki/Western_Wall" title="Western Wall">Western Wall</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Temple_Mount" title="Temple Mount">Temple Mount</a> (Al-Aqsa Mosque compound) and the <a href="/wiki/Church_of_the_Holy_Sepulchre" title="Church of the Holy Sepulchre">Church of the Holy Sepulchre</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-361" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-361">&#91;354&#93;</a></sup> Other locations of religious importance in Israel are <a href="/wiki/Nazareth" title="Nazareth">Nazareth</a> (holy in Christianity as the site of the <a href="/wiki/Annunciation" title="Annunciation">Annunciation</a> of <a href="/wiki/Mary_(mother_of_Jesus)" class="mw-redirect" title="Mary (mother of Jesus)">Mary</a>), <a href="/wiki/Tiberias" title="Tiberias">Tiberias</a> and <a href="/wiki/Safed" title="Safed">Safed</a> (two of the <a href="/wiki/Four_Holy_Cities" title="Four Holy Cities">Four Holy Cities</a> in Judaism), the <a href="/wiki/White_Mosque,_Ramla" class="mw-redirect" title="White Mosque, Ramla">White Mosque</a> in <a href="/wiki/Ramla" title="Ramla">Ramla</a> (holy in Islam as the shrine of the prophet <a href="/wiki/Salih" class="mw-redirect" title="Salih">Saleh</a>), and the <a href="/wiki/Church_of_Saint_George_and_Mosque_of_Al-Khadr,_Lod" class="mw-redirect" title="Church of Saint George and Mosque of Al-Khadr, Lod">Church of Saint George and Mosque of Al-Khadr, Lod</a> (holy in Christianity and Islam as the tomb of <a href="/wiki/Saint_George" title="Saint George">Saint George</a> or <a href="/wiki/Al_Khidr" class="mw-redirect" title="Al Khidr">Al Khidr</a>). A number of other religious landmarks are located in the <a href="/wiki/West_Bank" title="West Bank">West Bank</a>, among them <a href="/wiki/Joseph%27s_Tomb" title="Joseph&#39;s Tomb">Joseph's Tomb</a> in <a href="/wiki/Nablus" title="Nablus">Nablus</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Church_of_the_Nativity" title="Church of the Nativity">birthplace of Jesus</a> and <a href="/wiki/Rachel%27s_Tomb" title="Rachel&#39;s Tomb">Rachel's Tomb</a> in <a href="/wiki/Bethlehem" title="Bethlehem">Bethlehem</a>, and the <a href="/wiki/Cave_of_the_Patriarchs" title="Cave of the Patriarchs">Cave of the Patriarchs</a> in <a href="/wiki/Hebron" title="Hebron">Hebron</a>. The <a href="/wiki/Arc_(Bah%C3%A1%CA%BC%C3%AD)" class="mw-redirect" title="Arc (Baháʼí)">administrative center</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Bah%C3%A1%CA%BC%C3%AD_Faith" title="Baháʼí Faith">Baháʼí Faith</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Shrine_of_the_B%C3%A1b" title="Shrine of the Báb">Shrine of the Báb</a> are located at the <a href="/wiki/Bah%C3%A1%CA%BC%C3%AD_World_Centre" title="Baháʼí World Centre">Baháʼí World Centre</a> in <a href="/wiki/Haifa" title="Haifa">Haifa</a>; the leader of the faith is <a href="/wiki/Shrine_of_Bah%C3%A1%27u%27ll%C3%A1h" class="mw-redirect" title="Shrine of Bahá&#39;u&#39;lláh">buried</a> in <a href="/wiki/Acre,_Israel" title="Acre, Israel">Acre</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-362" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-362">&#91;355&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-363" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-363">&#91;356&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-364" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-364">&#91;357&#93;</a></sup> A few kilometres south of the Baháʼí World Centre is <a href="/wiki/Mahmood_Mosque,_Haifa" title="Mahmood Mosque, Haifa">Mahmood Mosque</a> affiliated with the reformist <a href="/wiki/Ahmadiyya_in_Israel" title="Ahmadiyya in Israel">Ahmadiyya</a> movement. <a href="/wiki/Kababir" title="Kababir">Kababir</a>, Haifa's mixed neighbourhood of Jews and Ahmadi Arabs is one of a few of its kind in the country, others being <a href="/wiki/Jaffa" title="Jaffa">Jaffa</a>, <a href="/wiki/Acre,_Israel" title="Acre, Israel">Acre</a>, other <a href="/wiki/Haifa" title="Haifa">Haifa</a> neighbourhoods, <a href="/wiki/Harish,_Israel" title="Harish, Israel">Harish</a> and <a href="/wiki/Upper_Nazareth" class="mw-redirect" title="Upper Nazareth">Upper Nazareth</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-365" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-365">&#91;358&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-366" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-366">&#91;359&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Education">Education</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Education_in_Israel" title="Education in Israel">Education in Israel</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Brain_research_labs-Bar_Ilan_university.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/09/Brain_research_labs-Bar_Ilan_university.jpg/220px-Brain_research_labs-Bar_Ilan_university.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="146" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/09/Brain_research_labs-Bar_Ilan_university.jpg/330px-Brain_research_labs-Bar_Ilan_university.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/09/Brain_research_labs-Bar_Ilan_university.jpg/440px-Brain_research_labs-Bar_Ilan_university.jpg 2x" data-file-width="700" data-file-height="463" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Bar-Ilan_University#Leslie_and_Susan_Gonda_Multidisciplinary_Brain_Research_Center" title="Bar-Ilan University">Multidisciplinary Brain Research Center</a> at <a href="/wiki/Bar-Ilan_University" title="Bar-Ilan University">Bar-Ilan University</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>Education is highly valued in the Israeli culture and was viewed as a <a href="/wiki/History_of_education_in_ancient_Israel_and_Judah" title="History of education in ancient Israel and Judah">fundamental block of ancient Israelites</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-367" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-367">&#91;360&#93;</a></sup> Jewish communities in the Levant were the first to introduce <a href="/wiki/Compulsory_education" title="Compulsory education">compulsory education</a> for which the organized community, not less than the parents was responsible.<sup id="cite_ref-368" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-368">&#91;361&#93;</a></sup> Many international business leaders such as Microsoft founder <a href="/wiki/Bill_Gates" title="Bill Gates">Bill Gates</a> have praised Israel for its high quality of education in helping spur Israel's economic development and technological boom.<sup id="cite_ref-David_Adler_369-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-David_Adler-369">&#91;362&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-370" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-370">&#91;363&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-371" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-371">&#91;364&#93;</a></sup> In 2015, the country <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_tertiary_education_attainment" title="List of countries by tertiary education attainment">ranked</a> third among <a href="/wiki/Organisation_for_Economic_Co-operation_and_Development" class="mw-redirect" title="Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development">OECD</a> members (after Canada and Japan) for the percentage of 25–64 year-olds that have attained <a href="/wiki/Tertiary_education" title="Tertiary education">tertiary education</a> with 49% compared with the OECD average of 35%.<sup id="cite_ref-OECD_education_372-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-OECD_education-372">&#91;365&#93;</a></sup> In 2012, the country ranked third in the world in the number of academic degrees per capita (20 percent of the population).<sup id="cite_ref-373" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-373">&#91;366&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Israel has a <a href="/wiki/School_life_expectancy" title="School life expectancy">school life expectancy</a> of 16 years and a <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_literacy_rate" title="List of countries by literacy rate">literacy rate</a> of 97.8%.<sup id="cite_ref-cia_280-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cia-280">&#91;273&#93;</a></sup> The State Education Law, passed in 1953, established five types of schools: state secular, state religious, ultra orthodox, communal settlement schools, and Arab schools. The public secular is the largest school group, and is attended by the majority of Jewish and non-Arab pupils in Israel. Most Arabs send their children to schools where Arabic is the language of instruction.<sup id="cite_ref-374" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-374">&#91;367&#93;</a></sup> Education is compulsory in Israel for children between the ages of three and eighteen.<sup id="cite_ref-375" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-375">&#91;368&#93;</a></sup> Schooling is divided into three tiers&#160;– primary school (grades 1–6), <a href="/wiki/Middle_school" title="Middle school">middle school</a> (grades 7–9), and high school (grades 10–12)&#160;– culminating with <i><a href="/wiki/Bagrut" class="mw-redirect" title="Bagrut">Bagrut</a></i> matriculation exams. Proficiency in core subjects such as mathematics, the <a href="/wiki/Hebrew_language" title="Hebrew language">Hebrew language</a>, Hebrew and general literature, the <a href="/wiki/English_language" title="English language">English language</a>, history, Biblical scripture and civics is necessary to receive a Bagrut certificate.<sup id="cite_ref-moia_376-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-moia-376">&#91;369&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Israel's Jewish population maintains a relatively high level of educational attainment where just under half of all Israeli Jews (46%) hold post-secondary degrees. This figure has remained stable in their already high levels of educational attainment over recent generations.<sup id="cite_ref-377" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-377">&#91;370&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-378" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-378">&#91;371&#93;</a></sup> Israeli Jews (among those ages 25 and older) have average of 11.6 years of schooling making them one of the most highly educated of all major religious groups in the world.<sup id="cite_ref-379" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-379">&#91;372&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-380" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-380">&#91;373&#93;</a></sup> In Arab, Christian and <a href="/wiki/Druze" title="Druze">Druze</a> schools, the exam on Biblical studies is replaced by an exam on Muslim, Christian or Druze heritage.<sup id="cite_ref-381" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-381">&#91;374&#93;</a></sup> <i><a href="/wiki/Maariv_(newspaper)" title="Maariv (newspaper)">Maariv</a></i> described the <a href="/wiki/Christian_Arabs" class="mw-redirect" title="Christian Arabs">Christian Arabs</a> sectors as "the most successful in education system",<sup id="cite_ref-המגזר_הערבי_נוצרי_הכי_מצליח_במערכת_החינוך_382-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-המגזר_הערבי_נוצרי_הכי_מצליח_במערכת_החינוך-382">&#91;375&#93;</a></sup> since Christians fared the best in terms of education in comparison to any other religion in Israel.<sup id="cite_ref-Christians_in_Israel:_Strong_in_education_383-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Christians_in_Israel:_Strong_in_education-383">&#91;376&#93;</a></sup> Israeli children from Russian-speaking families have a higher bagrut pass rate at high-school level.<sup id="cite_ref-384" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-384">&#91;377&#93;</a></sup> Amongst immigrant children born in the <a href="/wiki/Former_Soviet_Union" class="mw-redirect" title="Former Soviet Union">former Soviet Union</a>, the bagrut pass rate is higher amongst those families from European FSU states at 62.6% and lower amongst those from Central Asian and Caucasian FSU states.<sup id="cite_ref-385" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-385">&#91;378&#93;</a></sup> In 2014, 61.5% of all Israeli twelfth graders earned a matriculation certificate.<sup id="cite_ref-386" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-386">&#91;379&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Hebrew_University_Jerusalem_IL_WV.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/41/Hebrew_University_Jerusalem_IL_WV.JPG/220px-Hebrew_University_Jerusalem_IL_WV.JPG" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/41/Hebrew_University_Jerusalem_IL_WV.JPG/330px-Hebrew_University_Jerusalem_IL_WV.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/41/Hebrew_University_Jerusalem_IL_WV.JPG/440px-Hebrew_University_Jerusalem_IL_WV.JPG 2x" data-file-width="1000" data-file-height="750" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Mount_Scopus" title="Mount Scopus">Mount Scopus</a> Campus of the <a href="/wiki/Hebrew_University_of_Jerusalem" title="Hebrew University of Jerusalem">Hebrew University of Jerusalem</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>Israel has a tradition of higher education where its quality university education has been largely responsible in spurring the nation's modern economic development.<sup id="cite_ref-387" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-387">&#91;380&#93;</a></sup> Israel has <a href="/wiki/List_of_Israeli_universities_and_colleges" title="List of Israeli universities and colleges">nine public universities that are subsidized by the state and 49 private colleges</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-moia_376-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-moia-376">&#91;369&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-388" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-388">&#91;381&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-389" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-389">&#91;382&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Hebrew_University_of_Jerusalem" title="Hebrew University of Jerusalem">Hebrew University of Jerusalem</a>, Israel's second-oldest university after the <a href="/wiki/Technion" class="mw-redirect" title="Technion">Technion</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-390" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-390">&#91;383&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-391" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-391">&#91;384&#93;</a></sup> houses the <a href="/wiki/National_Library_of_Israel" title="National Library of Israel">National Library of Israel</a>, the world's largest repository of Judaica and Hebraica.<sup id="cite_ref-392" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-392">&#91;385&#93;</a></sup> The Technion and the Hebrew University consistently ranked among world's 100 top universities by the prestigious <a href="/wiki/Academic_Ranking_of_World_Universities" title="Academic Ranking of World Universities">ARWU</a> academic ranking.<sup id="cite_ref-ARWU_393-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ARWU-393">&#91;386&#93;</a></sup> Other major universities in the country include the <a href="/wiki/Weizmann_Institute_of_Science" title="Weizmann Institute of Science">Weizmann Institute of Science</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tel_Aviv_University" title="Tel Aviv University">Tel Aviv University</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ben-Gurion_University_of_the_Negev" title="Ben-Gurion University of the Negev">Ben-Gurion University of the Negev</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bar-Ilan_University" title="Bar-Ilan University">Bar-Ilan University</a>, the <a href="/wiki/University_of_Haifa" title="University of Haifa">University of Haifa</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Open_University_of_Israel" title="Open University of Israel">Open University of Israel</a>. <a href="/wiki/Ariel_University" title="Ariel University">Ariel University</a>, in the <a href="/wiki/West_Bank" title="West Bank">West Bank</a>, is the newest university institution, upgraded from college status, and the first in over thirty years.
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Government_and_politics">Government and politics</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Israeli_system_of_government" title="Israeli system of government">Israeli system of government</a> and <a href="/wiki/Politics_of_Israel" title="Politics of Israel">Politics of Israel</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Criticism_of_the_Israeli_government" class="mw-redirect" title="Criticism of the Israeli government">Criticism of the Israeli government</a></div>
<figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Israel%27s_political_system.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/83/Israel%27s_political_system.svg/300px-Israel%27s_political_system.svg.png" decoding="async" width="300" height="227" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/83/Israel%27s_political_system.svg/450px-Israel%27s_political_system.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/83/Israel%27s_political_system.svg/600px-Israel%27s_political_system.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="813" data-file-height="616" /></a><figcaption>Political system of Israel</figcaption></figure>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1096954695/mw-parser-output/.tmulti"><div class="thumb tmulti tright"><div class="thumbinner multiimageinner" title="Benjamin Netanyahu">Benjamin Netanyahu</a></div></div></div></div></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:PikiWiki_Israel_7260_Knesset-Room.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/13/PikiWiki_Israel_7260_Knesset-Room.jpg/220px-PikiWiki_Israel_7260_Knesset-Room.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/13/PikiWiki_Israel_7260_Knesset-Room.jpg/330px-PikiWiki_Israel_7260_Knesset-Room.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/13/PikiWiki_Israel_7260_Knesset-Room.jpg/440px-PikiWiki_Israel_7260_Knesset-Room.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1500" data-file-height="1000" /></a><figcaption>The <a href="/wiki/Knesset" title="Knesset">Knesset</a> chamber, home to the Israeli parliament</figcaption></figure>
<p>Israel is a <a href="/wiki/Parliamentary_democracy" class="mw-redirect" title="Parliamentary democracy">parliamentary democracy</a> with <a href="/wiki/Universal_suffrage" title="Universal suffrage">universal suffrage</a>. A member of parliament supported by a parliamentary majority becomes the <a href="/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Israel" title="Prime Minister of Israel">prime minister</a>—usually this is the chair of the largest party. The prime minister is the <a href="/wiki/Head_of_government" title="Head of government">head of government</a> and head of the <a href="/wiki/Cabinet_of_Israel" title="Cabinet of Israel">cabinet</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-cia2_394-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cia2-394">&#91;387&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-395" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-395">&#91;388&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Israel is governed by a 120-member parliament, known as the <a href="/wiki/Knesset" title="Knesset">Knesset</a>. Membership of the Knesset is based on <a href="/wiki/Proportional_representation" title="Proportional representation">proportional representation</a> of <a href="/wiki/List_of_political_parties_in_Israel" title="List of political parties in Israel">political parties</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-396" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-396">&#91;389&#93;</a></sup><sup class="noprint Inline-Template noprint noexcerpt Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:NOTRS" class="mw-redirect" title="Wikipedia:NOTRS"><span title="This claim needs references to better sources. (February 2023)">better&#160;source&#160;needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup> with a 3.25% electoral threshold, which in practice has resulted in coalition governments. Residents of Israeli settlements in the West Bank are eligible to vote<sup id="cite_ref-397" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-397">&#91;390&#93;</a></sup> and after the <a href="/wiki/2015_Israeli_legislative_election" title="2015 Israeli legislative election">2015 election</a>, 10 of the 120 MKs (<span data-sort-value="7000833333333333333♠" style="display:none"></span>8%) were settlers.<sup id="cite_ref-398" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-398">&#91;391&#93;</a></sup> Parliamentary <a href="/wiki/Elections_in_Israel" title="Elections in Israel">elections</a> are scheduled every four years, but unstable coalitions or a <a href="/wiki/Motion_of_no_confidence" title="Motion of no confidence">no-confidence vote</a> by the Knesset can dissolve a government earlier.<sup id="cite_ref-cnn_29-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cnn-29">&#91;23&#93;</a></sup> The first Arab-led party was established in 1988<sup id="cite_ref-399" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-399">&#91;392&#93;</a></sup> and as of 2022, Arab-led parties hold about 10% of the parliament's seats.<sup id="cite_ref-400" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-400">&#91;393&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Basic_Laws_of_Israel" title="Basic Laws of Israel">Basic Laws of Israel</a> function as an <a href="/wiki/Uncodified_constitution" title="Uncodified constitution">uncodified constitution</a>. In its <a href="/wiki/Basic_Laws_of_Israel" title="Basic Laws of Israel">Basic Laws</a>, Israel defines itself as a <a href="/wiki/Jewish_and_democratic_state" title="Jewish and democratic state">Jewish and democratic state</a>, and as the <a href="/wiki/Basic_Law:_Israel_as_the_Nation-State_of_the_Jewish_People" title="Basic Law: Israel as the Nation-State of the Jewish People">nation-state of the Jewish people</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-freedomhouse2008_401-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-freedomhouse2008-401">&#91;394&#93;</a></sup> In 2003, the Knesset began to draft an official <a href="/wiki/Constitution_of_Israel" class="mw-redirect" title="Constitution of Israel">constitution</a> based on these laws.<sup id="cite_ref-cia_280-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cia-280">&#91;273&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-402" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-402">&#91;395&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/President_of_Israel" title="President of Israel">president of Israel</a> is <a href="/wiki/Head_of_state" title="Head of state">head of state</a>, with limited and largely ceremonial duties.<sup id="cite_ref-cia2_394-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cia2-394">&#91;387&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Israel has no official religion,<sup id="cite_ref-403" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-403">&#91;396&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-404" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-404">&#91;397&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-405" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-405">&#91;398&#93;</a></sup> but the definition of the state as "<a href="/wiki/Jewish_and_democratic_state" title="Jewish and democratic state">Jewish and democratic</a>" creates a strong connection with Judaism, as well as a conflict between state law and religious law. Interaction between the political parties keeps <a href="/wiki/Status_quo_(Israel)" title="Status quo (Israel)">the balance</a> between state and religion largely as it existed during the British Mandate.<sup id="cite_ref-406" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-406">&#91;399&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 19 July 2018, the <a href="/wiki/Knesset" title="Knesset">Knesset</a> passed a Basic Law that characterizes the State of Israel as principally a "<a href="/wiki/Basic_Law:_Israel_as_the_Nation-State_of_the_Jewish_People" title="Basic Law: Israel as the Nation-State of the Jewish People">Nation State of the Jewish People</a>", and Hebrew as its official language. The bill ascribes "special status" to the Arabic language. The same bill gives Jews a unique right to national self-determination, and views the developing of Jewish settlement in the country as "a national interest", empowering the government to "take steps to encourage, advance and implement this interest."<sup id="cite_ref-407" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-407">&#91;400&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Legal_system">Legal system</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Judiciary_of_Israel" title="Judiciary of Israel">Judiciary of Israel</a> and <a href="/wiki/Israeli_law" title="Israeli law">Israeli law</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Israel_Supreme_Court.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e2/Israel_Supreme_Court.jpg/220px-Israel_Supreme_Court.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="144" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e2/Israel_Supreme_Court.jpg/330px-Israel_Supreme_Court.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e2/Israel_Supreme_Court.jpg/440px-Israel_Supreme_Court.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4217" data-file-height="2767" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_Israel" title="Supreme Court of Israel">Supreme Court of Israel</a>, Givat Ram, Jerusalem</figcaption></figure>
<p>Israel has a <a href="/wiki/Israeli_judicial_system" class="mw-redirect" title="Israeli judicial system">three-tier court system</a>. At the lowest level are <a href="/wiki/Magistrate" title="Magistrate">magistrate</a> courts, situated in most cities across the country. Above them are <a href="/wiki/District_court" title="District court">district courts</a>, serving as both <a href="/wiki/Appeal" title="Appeal">appellate</a> courts and <a href="/wiki/Trial_court" title="Trial court">courts of first instance</a>; they are situated in five of Israel's six <a href="/wiki/Districts_of_Israel" title="Districts of Israel">districts</a>. The third and highest tier is the <a href="/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_Israel" title="Supreme Court of Israel">Supreme Court</a>, located in Jerusalem; it serves a dual role as the highest court of appeals and the <a href="/wiki/High_Court_of_Justice_(Israel)" class="mw-redirect" title="High Court of Justice (Israel)">High Court of Justice</a>. In the latter role, the Supreme Court rules as a court of first instance, allowing individuals, both citizens and non-citizens, to petition against the decisions of state authorities.<sup id="cite_ref-408" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-408">&#91;401&#93;</a></sup> Although Israel supports the goals of the <a href="/wiki/International_Criminal_Court" title="International Criminal Court">International Criminal Court</a>, it has not ratified the <a href="/wiki/Rome_Statute_of_the_International_Criminal_Court" class="mw-redirect" title="Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court">Rome Statute</a>, citing concerns about the ability of the court to remain free from political impartiality.<sup id="cite_ref-409" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-409">&#91;402&#93;</a></sup><sup class="noprint Inline-Template noprint noexcerpt Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:NOTRS" class="mw-redirect" title="Wikipedia:NOTRS"><span title="This claim needs references to better sources. (January 2023)">better&#160;source&#160;needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup>
</p><p>Israel's legal system combines three legal traditions: <a href="/wiki/English_law" title="English law">English</a> <a href="/wiki/Common_law" title="Common law">common law</a>, <a href="/wiki/Civil_law_(legal_system)" title="Civil law (legal system)">civil law</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Halakha" title="Halakha">Jewish law</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-cia_280-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cia-280">&#91;273&#93;</a></sup> It is based on the principle of <i><a href="/wiki/Stare_decisis" class="mw-redirect" title="Stare decisis">stare decisis</a></i> (precedent) and is an <a href="/wiki/Adversarial_system" title="Adversarial system">adversarial system</a>, where the parties in the suit bring evidence before the court. Court cases are decided by professional judges with no role for juries.<sup id="cite_ref-judiciary_410-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-judiciary-410">&#91;403&#93;</a></sup><sup class="noprint Inline-Template noprint noexcerpt Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:NOTRS" class="mw-redirect" title="Wikipedia:NOTRS"><span title="This claim needs references to better sources. (January 2023)">better&#160;source&#160;needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup> <a href="/wiki/Marriage_in_Israel" title="Marriage in Israel">Marriage</a> and divorce are under the jurisdiction of the religious courts: <a href="/wiki/Beth_din" title="Beth din">Jewish</a>, <a href="/wiki/Sharia" title="Sharia">Muslim</a>, Druze, and Christian. The election of judges is carried out by a <a href="/wiki/Judicial_Selection_Committee_(Israel)" title="Judicial Selection Committee (Israel)">committee</a> of two Knesset members, three Supreme Court justices, two <a href="/wiki/Israel_Bar_Association" title="Israel Bar Association">Israeli Bar</a> members and two ministers (one of which, Israel's <a href="/wiki/Ministry_of_Justice_(Israel)" title="Ministry of Justice (Israel)">justice minister</a>, is the committee's chairman). The committee's members of the Knesset are <a href="/wiki/Secret_ballot" title="Secret ballot">secretly elected</a> by the Knesset, and one of them is traditionally a member of the opposition; the committee's Supreme Court justices are chosen by tradition from all Supreme Court justices by seniority; the Israeli Bar members are elected by the bar; and the second minister is appointed by the Israeli cabinet. The current justice minister, and the committee's chairman, is <a href="/wiki/Yariv_Levin" title="Yariv Levin">Yariv Levin</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-411" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-411">&#91;404&#93;</a></sup> Administration of Israel's courts (both the "General" courts and the <a href="/wiki/Labor_Courts_of_Israel" title="Labor Courts of Israel">Labor Courts</a>) is carried by the Administration of Courts, situated in Jerusalem. Both General and Labor courts are paperless courts: the storage of court files, as well as court decisions, are conducted electronically. Israel's <a href="/wiki/Basic_Law:_Human_Dignity_and_Liberty" title="Basic Law: Human Dignity and Liberty">Basic Law: Human Dignity and Liberty</a> seeks to defend <a href="/wiki/Human_rights_in_Israel" title="Human rights in Israel">human rights and liberties in Israel</a>. As a result of "<a href="/wiki/Enclave_law" class="mw-redirect" title="Enclave law">Enclave law</a>", large portions of Israeli <a href="/wiki/Civil_law_(legal_system)" title="Civil law (legal system)">civil law</a> are applied to Israeli settlements and Israeli residents in the occupied territories.<sup id="cite_ref-Ben-NaftaliSfard2018_412-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ben-NaftaliSfard2018-412">&#91;405&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Administrative_divisions">Administrative divisions</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Districts_of_Israel" title="Districts of Israel">Districts of Israel</a></div>
<div role="img" class="floatright noresize" style="width: 220px; line-height: 1; text-align: center; background-color: #ffffff; position: relative;"><span typeof="mw:File"><span><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/17/Israel_location_map.svg/220px-Israel_location_map.svg.png" decoding="async" width="220" height="409" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/17/Israel_location_map.svg/330px-Israel_location_map.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/17/Israel_location_map.svg/440px-Israel_location_map.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="614" data-file-height="1141" /></span></span>
