<div style="position:absolute; left:2.8px; top:388px"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1129693374"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1063604349"><div class="navbar plainlinks hlist navbar-mini"><ul><li class="nv-view"><a href="/wiki/Template:Israel_Labelled_Map" title="Template:Israel Labelled Map"><abbr title="View this template">v</abbr></a></li><li class="nv-talk"><a href="/wiki/Template_talk:Israel_Labelled_Map" title="Template talk:Israel Labelled Map"><abbr title="Discuss this template">t</abbr></a></li><li class="nv-edit"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Template:Israel_Labelled_Map&amp;action=edit"><abbr title="Edit this template">e</abbr></a></li></ul></div></div>
</div>
<p>The State of Israel is divided into six main administrative <a href="/wiki/Districts_of_Israel" title="Districts of Israel">districts</a>, known as <i>mehozot</i> (Hebrew: <span lang="he" dir="rtl">מחוזות</span>; singular: <i>mahoz</i>)&#160;– <a href="/wiki/Central_District_(Israel)" title="Central District (Israel)">Center</a>, <a href="/wiki/Haifa_District" title="Haifa District">Haifa</a>, <a href="/wiki/Jerusalem_District" title="Jerusalem District">Jerusalem</a>, <a href="/wiki/Northern_District_(Israel)" title="Northern District (Israel)">North</a>, <a href="/wiki/Southern_District_(Israel)" title="Southern District (Israel)">South</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Tel_Aviv_District" title="Tel Aviv District">Tel Aviv</a> districts, as well as the <a href="/wiki/Judea_and_Samaria_Area" title="Judea and Samaria Area">Judea and Samaria Area</a> in the <a href="/wiki/West_Bank" title="West Bank">West Bank</a>. All of the Judea and Samaria Area and parts of the Jerusalem and Northern districts are not recognized internationally as part of Israel. Districts are further divided into fifteen sub-districts known as <i>nafot</i> (Hebrew: <span lang="he" dir="rtl">נפות</span>; singular: <i>nafa</i>), which are themselves partitioned into fifty natural regions.<sup id="cite_ref-413" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-413">&#91;406&#93;</a></sup>
</p>

<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Map_of_Israel,_neighbours_and_occupied_territories.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/26/Map_of_Israel%2C_neighbours_and_occupied_territories.svg/300px-Map_of_Israel%2C_neighbours_and_occupied_territories.svg.png" decoding="async" width="300" height="387" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/26/Map_of_Israel%2C_neighbours_and_occupied_territories.svg/450px-Map_of_Israel%2C_neighbours_and_occupied_territories.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/26/Map_of_Israel%2C_neighbours_and_occupied_territories.svg/600px-Map_of_Israel%2C_neighbours_and_occupied_territories.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="559" data-file-height="721" /></a><figcaption>Map of Israel showing the West Bank, the Gaza Strip, and the Golan Heights</figcaption></figure>
<p>In 1967, as a result of the <a href="/wiki/Six-Day_War" title="Six-Day War">Six-Day War</a>, Israel captured and <a href="/wiki/Israeli-occupied_territories" title="Israeli-occupied territories">occupied</a> the <a href="/wiki/West_Bank" title="West Bank">West Bank</a>, including <a href="/wiki/East_Jerusalem" title="East Jerusalem">East Jerusalem</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Gaza_Strip" title="Gaza Strip">Gaza Strip</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Golan_Heights" title="Golan Heights">Golan Heights</a>. Israel also captured the <a href="/wiki/Sinai_Peninsula" title="Sinai Peninsula">Sinai Peninsula</a>, but returned it to Egypt as part of the 1979 <a href="/wiki/Egypt%E2%80%93Israel_peace_treaty" title="Egypt–Israel peace treaty">Egypt–Israel peace treaty</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEBregman2002186–187_234-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBregman2002186–187-234">&#91;227&#93;</a></sup> Between 1982 and 2000, Israel occupied <a href="/wiki/Israeli_occupation_of_Southern_Lebanon" title="Israeli occupation of Southern Lebanon">part of southern Lebanon</a>, in what was known as the <a href="/wiki/South_Lebanon_Security_Belt" class="mw-redirect" title="South Lebanon Security Belt">Security Belt</a>. Since Israel's capture of these territories, <a href="/wiki/Israeli_settlement" title="Israeli settlement">Israeli settlements</a> and military installations have been built within each of them, except Lebanon.
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Golan_Heights_Law" title="Golan Heights Law">Golan Heights</a> and <a href="/wiki/Jerusalem_Law" title="Jerusalem Law">East Jerusalem</a> have been fully incorporated into Israel under Israeli law, but not under international law. Israel has applied civilian law to both areas and granted their inhabitants permanent residency status and the ability to <a href="/wiki/Israeli_nationality_law" class="mw-redirect" title="Israeli nationality law">apply for citizenship</a>. The UN Security Council has declared the annexation of the Golan Heights and East Jerusalem to be "null and void" and continues to view the territories as occupied.<sup id="cite_ref-414" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-414">&#91;407&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-415" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-415">&#91;408&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Positions_on_Jerusalem" class="mw-redirect" title="Positions on Jerusalem">status</a> of East Jerusalem in any future peace settlement has at times been a difficult issue in <a href="/wiki/Israeli%E2%80%93Palestinian_peace_process" title="Israeli–Palestinian peace process">negotiations</a> between Israeli governments and representatives of the Palestinians, as Israel views it as its sovereign territory, as well as part of its capital.
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:West_Bank_Fence_South_Hebron.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ea/West_Bank_Fence_South_Hebron.JPG/220px-West_Bank_Fence_South_Hebron.JPG" decoding="async" width="220" height="144" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ea/West_Bank_Fence_South_Hebron.JPG/330px-West_Bank_Fence_South_Hebron.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ea/West_Bank_Fence_South_Hebron.JPG/440px-West_Bank_Fence_South_Hebron.JPG 2x" data-file-width="770" data-file-height="504" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Israeli_West_Bank_barrier" title="Israeli West Bank barrier">Israeli West Bank barrier</a> is a separation barrier built by Israel along the Green Line and inside parts of the West Bank.</figcaption></figure>
<p>The West Bank excluding East Jerusalem is known in Israeli law as the <a href="/wiki/Judea_and_Samaria_Area" title="Judea and Samaria Area">Judea and Samaria Area</a>; the almost 400,000 Israeli settlers residing in the area are considered part of Israel's population, have Knesset representation, a <a href="/wiki/Enclave_law" class="mw-redirect" title="Enclave law">large part of Israel's civil and criminal laws</a> applied to them, and their output is considered part of Israel's economy.<sup id="cite_ref-Sher_416-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Sher-416">&#91;409&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-oecd_17-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-oecd-17">&#91;fn 4&#93;</a></sup> The land itself is not considered part of Israel under Israeli law, as Israel has consciously refrained from annexing the territory, without ever relinquishing its legal claim to the land or defining a border with the area.<sup id="cite_ref-Sher_416-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Sher-416">&#91;409&#93;</a></sup> There is no border between Israel-proper and the West Bank for Israeli vehicles. Israeli political opposition to annexation is primarily due to the perceived "demographic threat" of incorporating the West Bank's Palestinian population into Israel.<sup id="cite_ref-Sher_416-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Sher-416">&#91;409&#93;</a></sup> Outside of the Israeli settlements, the West Bank remains under direct Israeli military rule, and Palestinians in the area cannot become Israeli citizens. The international community maintains that Israel does not have sovereignty in the West Bank, and considers Israel's control of the area to be the longest military occupation in modern history.<sup id="cite_ref-occhist_419-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-occhist-419">&#91;412&#93;</a></sup> The West Bank <a href="/wiki/Jordanian_annexation_of_the_West_Bank" title="Jordanian annexation of the West Bank">was occupied and annexed</a> by Jordan in 1950, following the 1949 Armistice Agreements. Only Britain recognized this annexation and Jordan has since <a href="/wiki/Jordanian_disengagement_from_the_West_Bank" class="mw-redirect" title="Jordanian disengagement from the West Bank">ceded</a> its claim to the territory to the PLO. The <a href="/wiki/Demographics_of_the_Palestinian_territories" class="mw-redirect" title="Demographics of the Palestinian territories">population</a> are mainly <a href="/wiki/Palestinian_people" class="mw-redirect" title="Palestinian people">Palestinians</a>, including <a href="/wiki/Palestinian_refugee" class="mw-redirect" title="Palestinian refugee">refugees</a> of the <a href="/wiki/1948_Arab%E2%80%93Israeli_War" title="1948 Arab–Israeli War">1948 Arab–Israeli War</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-420" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-420">&#91;413&#93;</a></sup> From their occupation in 1967 until 1993, the Palestinians living in these territories were under <a href="/wiki/Coordinator_of_Government_Activities_in_the_Territories" title="Coordinator of Government Activities in the Territories">Israeli military administration</a>. Since the <a href="/wiki/Israel%E2%80%93Palestine_Liberation_Organization_letters_of_recognition" title="Israel–Palestine Liberation Organization letters of recognition">Israel–PLO letters of recognition</a>, most of the Palestinian population and <a href="/wiki/List_of_cities_administered_by_the_State_of_Palestine" class="mw-redirect" title="List of cities administered by the State of Palestine">cities</a> have been under the internal jurisdiction of the <a href="/wiki/Palestinian_National_Authority" title="Palestinian National Authority">Palestinian Authority</a>, and only partial Israeli military control, although Israel has on several occasions redeployed its <a href="/wiki/Israel_Defense_Forces" title="Israel Defense Forces">troops</a> and reinstated full military administration during periods of unrest. In response to increasing attacks during the <a href="/wiki/Second_Intifada" title="Second Intifada">Second Intifada</a>, the Israeli government started to construct the Israeli West Bank barrier.<sup id="cite_ref-421" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-421">&#91;414&#93;</a></sup> When completed, approximately 13% of the barrier will be constructed on the <a href="/wiki/Green_Line_(Israel)" title="Green Line (Israel)">Green Line</a> or in Israel with 87% inside the West Bank.<sup id="cite_ref-422" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-422">&#91;415&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-423" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-423">&#91;416&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Restricted_space_in_the_West_Bank,_Area_C.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8a/Restricted_space_in_the_West_Bank%2C_Area_C.png/180px-Restricted_space_in_the_West_Bank%2C_Area_C.png" decoding="async" width="180" height="256" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8a/Restricted_space_in_the_West_Bank%2C_Area_C.png/270px-Restricted_space_in_the_West_Bank%2C_Area_C.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8a/Restricted_space_in_the_West_Bank%2C_Area_C.png/360px-Restricted_space_in_the_West_Bank%2C_Area_C.png 2x" data-file-width="6523" data-file-height="9295" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Area_C_(West_Bank)" title="Area C (West Bank)">Area C</a> of the West Bank, controlled by Israel <a href="/wiki/West_Bank_Areas_in_the_Oslo_II_Accord" title="West Bank Areas in the Oslo II Accord">under Oslo Accords</a>, in blue and red, in December 2011</figcaption></figure>
<p>The Gaza Strip is considered to be a "foreign territory" under Israeli law; however, since Israel operates a land, air, and sea <a href="/wiki/Blockade_of_the_Gaza_Strip" title="Blockade of the Gaza Strip">blockade of the Gaza Strip</a>, together with Egypt, the international community considers Israel to be the occupying power. The Gaza Strip was <a href="/wiki/Occupation_of_the_Gaza_Strip_by_Egypt" class="mw-redirect" title="Occupation of the Gaza Strip by Egypt">occupied by Egypt</a> from 1948 to 1967 and then by Israel after 1967. In 2005, as part of <a href="/wiki/Israel%27s_unilateral_disengagement_plan" class="mw-redirect" title="Israel&#39;s unilateral disengagement plan">Israel's unilateral disengagement plan</a>, Israel removed all of its settlers and forces from the territory, however, it continues to maintain <a href="/wiki/Blockade_of_the_Gaza_Strip" title="Blockade of the Gaza Strip">control</a> of its airspace and waters. The international community, including numerous international humanitarian organizations and various bodies of the UN, consider Gaza to remain occupied.<sup id="cite_ref-424" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-424">&#91;417&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-425" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-425">&#91;418&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-426" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-426">&#91;419&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-427" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-427">&#91;420&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-428" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-428">&#91;421&#93;</a></sup> Following the <a href="/wiki/Battle_of_Gaza_(2007)" title="Battle of Gaza (2007)">2007 Battle of Gaza</a>, when <a href="/wiki/Governance_of_the_Gaza_Strip" title="Governance of the Gaza Strip">Hamas assumed power in the Gaza Strip</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-gaza_429-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-gaza-429">&#91;422&#93;</a></sup> Israel tightened its control of the Gaza crossings along <a href="/wiki/Israel%E2%80%93Gaza_barrier" class="mw-redirect" title="Israel–Gaza barrier">its border</a>, as well as by sea and air, and prevented persons from entering and exiting the area except for isolated cases it deemed humanitarian.<sup id="cite_ref-gaza_429-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-gaza-429">&#91;422&#93;</a></sup> Gaza has a <a href="/wiki/Gaza%E2%80%93Egypt_border" class="mw-redirect" title="Gaza–Egypt border">border with Egypt</a>, and an agreement between Israel, the European Union, and the PA governed how border crossing would take place (it was monitored by European observers).<sup id="cite_ref-430" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-430">&#91;423&#93;</a></sup> The application of democracy to its Palestinian citizens, and the selective application of Israeli democracy in the Israeli-controlled Palestinian territories, has been criticized.<sup id="cite_ref-Slater2020_431-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Slater2020-431">&#91;424&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-White2012_432-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-White2012-432">&#91;425&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h4><span class="mw-headline" id="International_opinion">International opinion</span></h4>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/International_Court_of_Justice" title="International Court of Justice">International Court of Justice</a>, principal judicial organ of the UN, said, in its <a href="/wiki/International_law_and_the_Arab%E2%80%93Israeli_conflict#Ruling_of_the_ICJ" title="International law and the Arab–Israeli conflict">2004 advisory opinion</a> on the legality of the construction of the <a href="/wiki/Israeli_West_Bank_barrier" title="Israeli West Bank barrier">Israeli West Bank barrier</a>, that the lands captured by Israel in the Six-Day War, including East Jerusalem, are occupied territory, and further found that the construction of the wall within the occupied Palestinian territory to violate international law.<sup id="cite_ref-433" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-433">&#91;426&#93;</a></sup> Most negotiations relating to the territories have been on the basis of <a href="/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council_Resolution_242" title="United Nations Security Council Resolution 242">UN Security Council Resolution 242</a>, which emphasizes "the inadmissibility of the acquisition of territory by war", and calls on Israel to withdraw from occupied territories in return for normalization of relations with Arab states, a principle known as "<a href="/wiki/Land_for_peace" title="Land for peace">Land for peace</a>".<sup id="cite_ref-434" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-434">&#91;427&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-435" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-435">&#91;428&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-436" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-436">&#91;429&#93;</a></sup> Israel has been criticized for engaging in systematic and widespread violations of <a href="/wiki/Human_rights_in_the_Israeli-occupied_territories" class="mw-redirect" title="Human rights in the Israeli-occupied territories">human rights in the occupied territories</a>, including the occupation itself,<sup id="cite_ref-437" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-437">&#91;430&#93;</a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/War_crime" title="War crime">war crimes</a> against civilians.<sup id="cite_ref-tny1_438-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-tny1-438">&#91;431&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-439" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-439">&#91;432&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-440" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-440">&#91;433&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-441" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-441">&#91;434&#93;</a></sup> The allegations include violations of international humanitarian law<sup id="cite_ref-442" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-442">&#91;435&#93;</a></sup> by the <a href="/wiki/United_Nations_Human_Rights_Council" title="United Nations Human Rights Council">UN Human Rights Council</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-443" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-443">&#91;436&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/U.S._State_Department" class="mw-redirect" title="U.S. State Department">U.S. State Department</a> has called reports of abuses of significant human rights of Palestinians 'credible' both within Israel<sup id="cite_ref-444" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-444">&#91;437&#93;</a></sup> and the occupied territories.<sup id="cite_ref-445" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-445">&#91;438&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Amnesty_International" title="Amnesty International">Amnesty International</a> and other NGOs have documented mass arbitrary arrests, torture, unlawful killings, systemic abuses and impunity<sup id="cite_ref-446" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-446">&#91;439&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-447" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-447">&#91;440&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-448" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-448">&#91;441&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-449" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-449">&#91;442&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-450" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-450">&#91;443&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-451" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-451">&#91;444&#93;</a></sup> in tandem with a denial of the right to <a href="/wiki/Palestinian_self-determination" title="Palestinian self-determination">Palestinian self-determination</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-452" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-452">&#91;445&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-453" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-453">&#91;446&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-454" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-454">&#91;447&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-455" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-455">&#91;448&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-456" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-456">&#91;449&#93;</a></sup> In response to such allegations, Prime Minister Netanyahu has defended the country's security forces for protecting the innocent from terrorists<sup id="cite_ref-457" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-457">&#91;450&#93;</a></sup> and expressed contempt for what he describes as a lack of concern about the human rights violations committed by "criminal killers".<sup id="cite_ref-458" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-458">&#91;451&#93;</a></sup> Some observers, such as Israeli officials, scholars,<sup id="cite_ref-459" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-459">&#91;452&#93;</a></sup> United States Ambassador to the UN <a href="/wiki/Nikki_Haley" title="Nikki Haley">Nikki Haley</a><sup id="cite_ref-460" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-460">&#91;453&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-461" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-461">&#91;454&#93;</a></sup> and UN secretary-generals <a href="/wiki/Ban_Ki-moon" title="Ban Ki-moon">Ban Ki-moon</a><sup id="cite_ref-462" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-462">&#91;455&#93;</a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/Kofi_Annan" title="Kofi Annan">Kofi Annan</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-463" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-463">&#91;456&#93;</a></sup> also assert that the UN is disproportionately concerned with Israeli misconduct.<sup class="noprint Inline-Template noprint Template-Opinion" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:TERSE" class="mw-redirect" title="Wikipedia:TERSE"><span title="Statements that may be excessive (April 2017)">excessive detail?</span></a></i>&#93;</sup>
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/International_community" title="International community">international community</a> widely regards Israeli settlements in the occupied territories <a href="/wiki/International_law_and_Israeli_settlements" title="International law and Israeli settlements">illegal under international law</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-464" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-464">&#91;457&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council_Resolution_2334" title="United Nations Security Council Resolution 2334">United Nations Security Council Resolution 2334</a>, passed on 23 December 2016 in a 14–0 vote by members of the <a href="/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council" title="United Nations Security Council">U.N. Security Council</a> (UNSC) with the United States abstaining. The resolution states that Israel's settlement activity constitutes a "flagrant violation" of <a href="/wiki/International_law" title="International law">international law</a>, has "no legal validity" and demands that Israel stop such activity and fulfill its obligations as an <a href="/wiki/Military_occupation#The_occupying_power" title="Military occupation">occupying power</a> under the <a href="/wiki/Fourth_Geneva_Convention" title="Fourth Geneva Convention">Fourth Geneva Convention</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-toi_465-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-toi-465">&#91;458&#93;</a></sup> A <a href="/wiki/United_Nations_special_rapporteur" title="United Nations special rapporteur">United Nations special rapporteur</a> concluded that settlement program was a <a href="/wiki/War_crime" title="War crime">war crime</a> under the <a href="/wiki/Rome_Statute" title="Rome Statute">Rome Statute</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-466" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-466">&#91;459&#93;</a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/Amnesty_International" title="Amnesty International">Amnesty International</a> found that the settlement program constitutes an illegal transfer of civilians into occupied territory as well as amounting to "pillage", which is prohibited by both the <a href="/wiki/Hague_Conventions_of_1899_and_1907" title="Hague Conventions of 1899 and 1907">Hague Conventions</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Geneva_Conventions" title="Geneva Conventions">Geneva Conventions</a> as well as being a war crime under the Rome Statute.<sup id="cite_ref-467" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-467">&#91;460&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h4><span class="mw-headline" id="Apartheid_accusations">Apartheid accusations</span></h4>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Israel_and_apartheid" title="Israel and apartheid">Israel and apartheid</a></div>
<p>Israel's treatment of the Palestinians within the occupied territories has drawn <a href="/wiki/Israel_and_apartheid" title="Israel and apartheid">accusations that it is guilty of</a> the <a href="/wiki/Crime_of_apartheid" title="Crime of apartheid">crime of apartheid</a> by Israeli human rights groups <a href="/wiki/Yesh_Din" title="Yesh Din">Yesh Din</a> and <a href="/wiki/B%27tselem" class="mw-redirect" title="B&#39;tselem">B'tselem</a>, and other international organizations including <a href="/wiki/Amnesty_International" title="Amnesty International">Amnesty International</a> and <a href="/wiki/Human_Rights_Watch" title="Human Rights Watch">Human Rights Watch</a>, with the criticism extending to its treatment of <a href="/wiki/Palestinian_citizens_of_Israel" title="Palestinian citizens of Israel">Palestinians within Israel</a> as well.<sup id="cite_ref-468" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-468">&#91;461&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-469" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-469">&#91;462&#93;</a></sup> Amnesty's report was criticized by politicians and government representatives from Israel, the United States, the United Kingdom, Netherlands and Germany, while it was welcomed by Palestinians, representatives from other states, and organizations such as the <a href="/wiki/Arab_League" title="Arab League">Arab League</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-470" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-470">&#91;463&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-471" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-471">&#91;464&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-472" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-472">&#91;465&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-473" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-473">&#91;466&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-474" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-474">&#91;467&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-475" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-475">&#91;468&#93;</a></sup> A 2021 survey of academic experts on the Middle East found an increase from 59%<sup id="cite_ref-476" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-476">&#91;469&#93;</a></sup> to 65% of these scholars describing Israel as a "one-state reality akin to apartheid".<sup id="cite_ref-477" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-477">&#91;470&#93;</a></sup> In 2022, Michael Lynk, a Canadian law professor <a href="/wiki/United_Nations_Special_Rapporteur_on_the_occupied_Palestinian_territories" title="United Nations Special Rapporteur on the occupied Palestinian territories">appointed by the U.N. Human Rights Council</a> said that the situation met the legal definition of apartheid.<sup id="cite_ref-478" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-478">&#91;471&#93;</a></sup> Subsequent reports from his successor, <a href="/wiki/Francesca_Albanese" title="Francesca Albanese">Francesca Albanese</a> and from  <a href="/wiki/Permanent_United_Nations_Fact_Finding_Mission_on_the_Israel_Palestine_conflict" title="Permanent United Nations Fact Finding Mission on the Israel Palestine conflict">Permanent United Nations Fact Finding Mission on the Israel Palestine conflict</a> chair Navi Pillay echoed this opinion.<sup id="cite_ref-479" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-479">&#91;472&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-480" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-480">&#91;473&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Crime_of_apartheid" title="Crime of apartheid">crime of apartheid</a> is a <a href="/wiki/Crime_against_humanity" class="mw-redirect" title="Crime against humanity">crime against humanity</a> under the Rome Statute and the <a href="/wiki/International_Convention_on_the_Suppression_and_Punishment_of_the_Crime_of_Apartheid" class="mw-redirect" title="International Convention on the Suppression and Punishment of the Crime of Apartheid">International Convention on the Suppression and Punishment of the Crime of Apartheid</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-481" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-481">&#91;474&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-482" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-482">&#91;475&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Foreign_relations">Foreign relations</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Foreign_relations_of_Israel" title="Foreign relations of Israel">Foreign relations of Israel</a> and <a href="/wiki/International_recognition_of_Israel" title="International recognition of Israel">International recognition of Israel</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Foreign_relations_of_Israel_(map).png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/32/Foreign_relations_of_Israel_%28map%29.png/300px-Foreign_relations_of_Israel_%28map%29.png" decoding="async" width="300" height="132" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/32/Foreign_relations_of_Israel_%28map%29.png/450px-Foreign_relations_of_Israel_%28map%29.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/32/Foreign_relations_of_Israel_%28map%29.png/600px-Foreign_relations_of_Israel_%28map%29.png 2x" data-file-width="1425" data-file-height="628" /></a><figcaption><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#0000ff; color:white;">&#160;</span>&#160;Diplomatic relations</div> <link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#80ffff; color:black;">&#160;</span>&#160;Diplomatic relations suspended</div> <link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#00ff00; color:black;">&#160;</span>&#160;Former diplomatic relations</div> <link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#ff00ff; color:black;">&#160;</span>&#160;No diplomatic relations, but former trade relations</div> <link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#ff8040; color:black;">&#160;</span>&#160;No diplomatic relations</div></figcaption></figure>
<p>Israel maintains diplomatic relations with&#160;164&#160;<a href="/wiki/United_Nations_member_states" class="mw-redirect" title="United Nations member states">member states</a> of the United Nations, as well as with the <a href="/wiki/Holy_See" title="Holy See">Holy See</a>, <a href="/wiki/Kosovo" title="Kosovo">Kosovo</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Cook_Islands" title="Cook Islands">Cook Islands</a> and <a href="/wiki/Niue" title="Niue">Niue</a>. It has 107 <a href="/wiki/List_of_diplomatic_missions_of_Israel" title="List of diplomatic missions of Israel">diplomatic missions</a> around the world;<sup id="cite_ref-483" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-483">&#91;476&#93;</a></sup> countries with whom they have no diplomatic relations include most Muslim countries.<sup id="cite_ref-484" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-484">&#91;477&#93;</a></sup> Six out of twenty-two nations in the <a href="/wiki/Arab_League" title="Arab League">Arab League</a> have normalized relations with Israel. <a href="/wiki/Egypt%E2%80%93Israel_relations" title="Egypt–Israel relations">Egypt</a> and <a href="/wiki/Israel%E2%80%93Jordan_relations" title="Israel–Jordan relations">Jordan</a> signed peace treaties in <a href="/wiki/Egypt%E2%80%93Israel_peace_treaty" title="Egypt–Israel peace treaty">1979</a> and <a href="/wiki/Israel%E2%80%93Jordan_Treaty_of_Peace" class="mw-redirect" title="Israel–Jordan Treaty of Peace">1994</a>, respectively, but Israel remains formally in a <a href="/wiki/Israel%E2%80%93Syria_relations" title="Israel–Syria relations">state of war with Syria</a>, a status that dates back uninterrupted to 1948. It has been in a similarly <a href="/wiki/Israel%E2%80%93Lebanon_relations" title="Israel–Lebanon relations">formal state of war with Lebanon</a> since the end of the <a href="/wiki/Lebanese_Civil_War" title="Lebanese Civil War">Lebanese Civil War</a> in 2000, with the Israel–Lebanon border remaining unagreed by treaty.
</p><p>In late 2020, Israel normalized relations with four more Arab countries: the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain in September (known as the <a href="/wiki/Abraham_Accords" title="Abraham Accords">Abraham Accords</a>),<sup id="cite_ref-485" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-485">&#91;478&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Israel%E2%80%93Sudan_normalization_agreement" title="Israel–Sudan normalization agreement">Sudan in October</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-486" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-486">&#91;479&#93;</a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/Israel%E2%80%93Morocco_normalization_agreement" title="Israel–Morocco normalization agreement">Morocco in December</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-487" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-487">&#91;480&#93;</a></sup> Despite the peace treaty between Israel and Egypt, Israel is still widely considered an enemy country among Egyptians.<sup id="cite_ref-488" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-488">&#91;481&#93;</a></sup> Iran <a href="/wiki/Iran%E2%80%93Israel_relations" title="Iran–Israel relations">had diplomatic relations</a> with Israel under the <a href="/wiki/Pahlavi_dynasty" title="Pahlavi dynasty">Pahlavi dynasty</a><sup id="cite_ref-489" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-489">&#91;482&#93;</a></sup> but withdrew its recognition of Israel during the <a href="/wiki/Islamic_Revolution" class="mw-redirect" title="Islamic Revolution">Islamic Revolution</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-490" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-490">&#91;483&#93;</a></sup> Israeli citizens may not visit Syria, Lebanon, Iraq, Saudi Arabia, and Yemen (countries Israel fought in the 1948 Arab–Israeli War that Israel does not have a peace treaty with) without permission from the <a href="/wiki/Ministry_of_Interior_(Israel)" title="Ministry of Interior (Israel)">Ministry of the Interior</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-491" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-491">&#91;484&#93;</a></sup> As a result of the <a href="/wiki/Gaza_War_(2008%E2%80%9309)" class="mw-redirect" title="Gaza War (2008–09)">2008–09 Gaza War</a>, Mauritania, Qatar, Bolivia, and Venezuela suspended political and economic ties with Israel,<sup id="cite_ref-al-jaz-eng_492-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-al-jaz-eng-492">&#91;485&#93;</a></sup> though Bolivia renewed ties in 2019.<sup id="cite_ref-493" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-493">&#91;486&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/China%E2%80%93Israel_relations" title="China–Israel relations">China</a> maintains good ties with both Israel and the Arab world.<sup id="cite_ref-494" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-494">&#91;487&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Bill_Clinton,_Yitzhak_Rabin,_Yasser_Arafat_at_the_White_House_1993-09-13.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f2/Bill_Clinton%2C_Yitzhak_Rabin%2C_Yasser_Arafat_at_the_White_House_1993-09-13.jpg/220px-Bill_Clinton%2C_Yitzhak_Rabin%2C_Yasser_Arafat_at_the_White_House_1993-09-13.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="150" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f2/Bill_Clinton%2C_Yitzhak_Rabin%2C_Yasser_Arafat_at_the_White_House_1993-09-13.jpg/330px-Bill_Clinton%2C_Yitzhak_Rabin%2C_Yasser_Arafat_at_the_White_House_1993-09-13.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f2/Bill_Clinton%2C_Yitzhak_Rabin%2C_Yasser_Arafat_at_the_White_House_1993-09-13.jpg/440px-Bill_Clinton%2C_Yitzhak_Rabin%2C_Yasser_Arafat_at_the_White_House_1993-09-13.jpg 2x" data-file-width="602" data-file-height="411" /></a><figcaption>Yitzhak Rabin and Yasser Arafat at the signing ceremony of the <a href="/wiki/Oslo_Accords" title="Oslo Accords">Oslo Accords</a> with then US President <a href="/wiki/Bill_Clinton" title="Bill Clinton">Bill Clinton</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/Israel%E2%80%93United_States_relations" title="Israel–United States relations">United States</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Israel%E2%80%93Russia_relations" title="Israel–Russia relations">Soviet Union</a> were the first two countries to recognize the State of Israel, having declared recognition roughly simultaneously.<sup id="cite_ref-495" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-495">&#91;488&#93;</a></sup> Diplomatic relations with the Soviet Union were broken in 1967, following the <a href="/wiki/Six-Day_War" title="Six-Day War">Six-Day War</a>, and renewed in October 1991.<sup id="cite_ref-496" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-496">&#91;489&#93;</a></sup> The United States regards Israel as its "most reliable partner in the Middle East",<sup id="cite_ref-497" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-497">&#91;490&#93;</a></sup> based on "common democratic values, religious affinities, and security interests".<sup id="cite_ref-498" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-498">&#91;491&#93;</a></sup> The United States has provided $68&#160;billion in <a href="/wiki/Israel%E2%80%93United_States_military_relations" title="Israel–United States military relations">military assistance</a> and $32&#160;billion in grants to Israel since 1967, under the <a href="/wiki/Foreign_Assistance_Act" title="Foreign Assistance Act">Foreign Assistance Act</a> (period beginning 1962),<sup id="cite_ref-PNADR900_499-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-PNADR900-499">&#91;492&#93;</a></sup> more than any other country for that period until 2003.<sup id="cite_ref-PNADR900_499-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-PNADR900-499">&#91;492&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-500" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-500">&#91;493&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-501" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-501">&#91;494&#93;</a></sup> Most surveyed Americans have also held consistently favorable views of Israel.<sup id="cite_ref-502" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-502">&#91;495&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-503" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-503">&#91;496&#93;</a></sup> The United Kingdom is seen as having a "natural" <a href="/wiki/Israel%E2%80%93United_Kingdom_relations" title="Israel–United Kingdom relations">relationship</a> with Israel on account of the Mandate for Palestine.<sup id="cite_ref-504" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-504">&#91;497&#93;</a></sup> Relations between the two countries were also made stronger by former prime minister <a href="/wiki/Tony_Blair" title="Tony Blair">Tony Blair</a>'s efforts for a two state resolution. By 2007<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Israel&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup>, <a href="/wiki/Germany%E2%80%93Israel_relations" title="Germany–Israel relations">Germany</a> had paid 25&#160;billion euros in <a href="/wiki/Reparations_Agreement_between_Israel_and_West_Germany" class="mw-redirect" title="Reparations Agreement between Israel and West Germany">reparations</a> to the Israeli state and individual Israeli Holocaust survivors.<sup id="cite_ref-505" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-505">&#91;498&#93;</a></sup> Israel is <a href="/wiki/Israel%E2%80%93European_Union_relations" title="Israel–European Union relations">included</a> in the European Union's <a href="/wiki/European_Neighbourhood_Policy" title="European Neighbourhood Policy">European Neighbourhood Policy</a> (ENP), which aims at bringing the EU and its neighbours closer.<sup id="cite_ref-506" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-506">&#91;499&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Although Turkey and Israel did not establish full diplomatic relations until 1991,<sup id="cite_ref-507" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-507">&#91;500&#93;</a></sup> Turkey has <a href="/wiki/Israel%E2%80%93Turkey_relations" title="Israel–Turkey relations">cooperated</a> with the Jewish state since its recognition of Israel in 1949. Turkey's ties to other Muslim-majority nations in the region have at times resulted in pressure from Arab and Muslim states to temper its relationship with Israel.<sup id="cite_ref-508" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-508">&#91;501&#93;</a></sup> Relations between Turkey and Israel took a downturn after the 2008–09 Gaza War and Israel's <a href="/wiki/Gaza_flotilla_raid" title="Gaza flotilla raid">raid of the Gaza flotilla</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-509" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-509">&#91;502&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Greece%E2%80%93Israel_relations" title="Greece–Israel relations">Relations between Greece and Israel</a> have improved since 1995 due to the decline of Israeli–Turkish relations.<sup id="cite_ref-510" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-510">&#91;503&#93;</a></sup> The two countries have a defense cooperation agreement and in 2010, the <a href="/wiki/Israeli_Air_Force" title="Israeli Air Force">Israeli Air Force</a> hosted Greece's <a href="/wiki/Hellenic_Air_Force" title="Hellenic Air Force">Hellenic Air Force</a> in a joint exercise at the <a href="/wiki/Ovda_Airport" title="Ovda Airport">Uvda base</a>. The joint Cyprus-Israel oil and gas explorations centered on the <a href="/wiki/Leviathan_gas_field" title="Leviathan gas field">Leviathan gas field</a> are an important factor for Greece, given its <a href="/wiki/Cyprus%E2%80%93Greece_relations" title="Cyprus–Greece relations">strong links</a> with Cyprus.<sup id="cite_ref-511" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-511">&#91;504&#93;</a></sup> Cooperation in the world's longest <a href="/wiki/Submarine_power_cable" title="Submarine power cable">subsea electric power cable</a>, the <a href="/wiki/EuroAsia_Interconnector" title="EuroAsia Interconnector">EuroAsia Interconnector</a>, has strengthened <a href="/wiki/Cyprus%E2%80%93Israel_relations" title="Cyprus–Israel relations">relations between Cyprus and Israel</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-512" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-512">&#91;505&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Azerbaijan" title="Azerbaijan">Azerbaijan</a> is one of the few majority Muslim countries to develop strategic and economic <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijan%E2%80%93Israel_relations" title="Azerbaijan–Israel relations">relations</a> with Israel.<sup id="cite_ref-:2_513-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:2-513">&#91;506&#93;</a></sup> Azerbaijan supplies the country with a substantial amount of its oil needs, and Israel is a critical arms supplier for Azerbaijan.<sup id="cite_ref-:2_513-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:2-513">&#91;506&#93;</a></sup> Kazakhstan also has an economic and strategic partnership with Israel.<sup id="cite_ref-514" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-514">&#91;507&#93;</a></sup> India established full <a href="/wiki/India%E2%80%93Israel_relations" title="India–Israel relations">diplomatic ties</a> with Israel in 1992 and has fostered a strong military, technological and cultural partnership with the country since then.<sup id="cite_ref-515" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-515">&#91;508&#93;</a></sup> A 2009 survey done on behalf of the <a href="/wiki/Ministry_of_Foreign_Affairs_(Israel)" title="Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Israel)">Israel Ministry of Foreign Affairs</a> listed India as more pro-Israel than 12 other countries surveyed.<sup id="cite_ref-516" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-516">&#91;509&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-517" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-517">&#91;510&#93;</a></sup> India is the largest customer of the <a href="/wiki/Israeli_military_equipment" class="mw-redirect" title="Israeli military equipment">Israeli military equipment</a> and Israel is the second-largest military partner of India after Russia.<sup id="cite_ref-518" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-518">&#91;511&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Ethiopia%E2%80%93Israel_relations" title="Ethiopia–Israel relations">Ethiopia</a> is Israel's main ally in Africa due to common political, religious and security interests.<sup id="cite_ref-519" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-519">&#91;512&#93;</a></sup> Israel provides expertise to Ethiopia on irrigation projects and thousands of <a href="/wiki/Ethiopian_Jews_in_Israel" title="Ethiopian Jews in Israel">Ethiopian Jews live in Israel</a>.
</p>
<h4><span class="mw-headline" id="Foreign_aid">Foreign aid</span></h4>
<p>Israel has a history of providing emergency <a href="/wiki/Israeli_foreign_aid" title="Israeli foreign aid">foreign aid</a> and humanitarian response teams to disasters across the world.<sup id="cite_ref-520" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-520">&#91;513&#93;</a></sup> In 1955 Israel began its foreign aid programme in Burma. The programme's focus subsequently shifted to Africa.<sup id="cite_ref-Geldenhuys_521-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Geldenhuys-521">&#91;514&#93;</a></sup> Israel's humanitarian efforts officially began in 1957, with the establishment of <a href="/wiki/Mashav" title="Mashav">Mashav</a>, the Israel's Agency for International Development Cooperation.<sup id="cite_ref-522" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-522">&#91;515&#93;</a></sup> In this early period, whilst Israel's aid represented only a small percentage of total aid to Africa, its programme was effective in creating goodwill throughout the continent; however, following the 1967 war relations soured.<sup id="cite_ref-Ismael_523-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ismael-523">&#91;516&#93;</a></sup> Israel's foreign aid programme subsequently shifted its focus to Latin America.<sup id="cite_ref-Geldenhuys_521-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Geldenhuys-521">&#91;514&#93;</a></sup> Since the late 1970s Israel's foreign aid has gradually decreased, although in recent years Israel has tried to reestablish its aid to Africa.<sup id="cite_ref-Yacobi_524-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Yacobi-524">&#91;517&#93;</a></sup> There are additional Israeli humanitarian and emergency response groups that work with the Israel government, including <a href="/wiki/IsraAid" title="IsraAid">IsraAid</a>, a joint programme run by 14 Israeli organizations and North American Jewish groups,<sup id="cite_ref-525" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-525">&#91;518&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/ZAKA" title="ZAKA">ZAKA</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-526" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-526">&#91;519&#93;</a></sup> The Fast Israeli Rescue and Search Team (FIRST),<sup id="cite_ref-527" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-527">&#91;520&#93;</a></sup> Israeli Flying Aid (IFA),<sup id="cite_ref-528" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-528">&#91;521&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Save_a_Child%27s_Heart" title="Save a Child&#39;s Heart">Save a Child's Heart</a> (SACH)<sup id="cite_ref-529" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-529">&#91;522&#93;</a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/Latet" title="Latet">Latet</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-530" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-530">&#91;523&#93;</a></sup> Between 1985 and 2015, Israel sent 24 delegations of IDF search and rescue unit, the <a href="/wiki/Home_Front_Command" title="Home Front Command">Home Front Command</a>, to 22 countries.<sup id="cite_ref-531" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-531">&#91;524&#93;</a></sup> Currently Israeli foreign aid <a href="/wiki/List_of_development_aid_country_donors" class="mw-redirect" title="List of development aid country donors">ranks</a> low among <a href="/wiki/Organisation_for_Economic_Co-operation_and_Development" class="mw-redirect" title="Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development">OECD</a> nations, spending less than 0.1% of its <a href="/wiki/Gross_national_income" title="Gross national income">GNI</a> on development assistance.<sup id="cite_ref-532" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-532">&#91;525&#93;</a></sup> The UN has set a target of 0.7%. In 2015 six nations reached the UN target.<sup id="cite_ref-Quinn_533-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Quinn-533">&#91;526&#93;</a></sup> The country ranked 38th in the 2018 <a href="/wiki/World_Giving_Index" title="World Giving Index">World Giving Index</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-534" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-534">&#91;527&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Military">Military</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Israel_Defense_Forces" title="Israel Defense Forces">Israel Defense Forces</a> and <a href="/wiki/Israeli_security_forces" title="Israeli security forces">Israeli security forces</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/List_of_wars_involving_Israel" title="List of wars involving Israel">List of wars involving Israel</a>, <a href="/wiki/List_of_the_Israel_Defense_Forces_operations" class="mw-redirect" title="List of the Israel Defense Forces operations">List of the Israel Defense Forces operations</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Israel_and_weapons_of_mass_destruction" title="Israel and weapons of mass destruction">Israel and weapons of mass destruction</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:The_Southern_Lions._Squadron_116._I.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/84/The_Southern_Lions._Squadron_116._I.jpg/220px-The_Southern_Lions._Squadron_116._I.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="143" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/84/The_Southern_Lions._Squadron_116._I.jpg/330px-The_Southern_Lions._Squadron_116._I.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/84/The_Southern_Lions._Squadron_116._I.jpg/440px-The_Southern_Lions._Squadron_116._I.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1600" data-file-height="1038" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/F-35" class="mw-redirect" title="F-35">F-35</a> fighter jets of the <a href="/wiki/Israeli_Air_Force" title="Israeli Air Force">Israeli Air Force</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/Israel_Defense_Forces" title="Israel Defense Forces">Israel Defense Forces</a> (IDF) is the sole military wing of the <a href="/wiki/Israeli_security_forces" title="Israeli security forces">Israeli security forces</a> and is headed by its <a href="/wiki/Chief_of_General_Staff_(Israel)" class="mw-redirect" title="Chief of General Staff (Israel)">Chief of General Staff</a>, the <i>Ramatkal</i>, subordinate to the <a href="/wiki/Cabinet_of_Israel" title="Cabinet of Israel">Cabinet</a>. The IDF consists of the <a href="/wiki/GOC_Army_Headquarters" title="GOC Army Headquarters">army</a>, <a href="/wiki/Israeli_Air_Force" title="Israeli Air Force">air force</a> and <a href="/wiki/Israeli_Navy" title="Israeli Navy">navy</a>. It was founded during the <a href="/wiki/1948_Arab%E2%80%93Israeli_War" title="1948 Arab–Israeli War">1948 Arab–Israeli War</a> by consolidating paramilitary organizations—chiefly the <a href="/wiki/Haganah" title="Haganah">Haganah</a>—that preceded the establishment of the state.<sup id="cite_ref-535" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-535">&#91;528&#93;</a></sup> The IDF also draws upon the resources of the <a href="/wiki/Military_Intelligence_Directorate_(Israel)" title="Military Intelligence Directorate (Israel)">Military Intelligence Directorate</a> (<i>Aman</i>), which works with <a href="/wiki/Mossad" title="Mossad">Mossad</a> and <a href="/wiki/Shin_Bet" title="Shin Bet">Shabak</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-536" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-536">&#91;529&#93;</a></sup> The Israel Defense Forces have been involved in several <a href="/wiki/List_of_wars_involving_Israel" title="List of wars involving Israel">major wars</a> and border conflicts in its short history, making it one of the most battle-trained armed forces in the world.<sup id="cite_ref-537" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-537">&#91;530&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Most Israelis are <a href="/wiki/Conscription_in_Israel" title="Conscription in Israel">drafted into the military</a> at the age of 18. Men serve two years and eight months and <a href="/wiki/Women_in_the_Israel_Defense_Forces" title="Women in the Israel Defense Forces">women</a> two years.<sup id="cite_ref-538" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-538">&#91;531&#93;</a></sup> Following mandatory service, Israeli men join the reserve forces and usually do up to several weeks of <a href="/wiki/Reserve_duty_(Israel)" title="Reserve duty (Israel)">reserve duty</a> every year until their forties. Most women are exempt from reserve duty. <a href="/wiki/Arab_citizens_of_Israel" title="Arab citizens of Israel">Arab citizens of Israel</a> (except the <a href="/wiki/Druze_in_Israel" title="Druze in Israel">Druze</a>) and those engaged in full-time religious studies are <a href="/wiki/Exemption_from_military_service_in_Israel" title="Exemption from military service in Israel">exempt from military service</a>, although the <a href="/wiki/Tal_committee" class="mw-redirect" title="Tal committee">exemption of yeshiva students</a> has been a source of contention in Israeli society for many years.<sup id="cite_ref-539" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-539">&#91;532&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-540" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-540">&#91;533&#93;</a></sup> An alternative for those who receive exemptions on various grounds is <i><a href="/wiki/Sherut_Leumi" title="Sherut Leumi">Sherut Leumi</a></i>, or national service, which involves a programme of service in hospitals, schools and other social welfare frameworks.<sup id="cite_ref-541" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-541">&#91;534&#93;</a></sup> A small minority of Israeli Arabs also volunteer to serve in the army.<sup id="cite_ref-542" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-542">&#91;535&#93;</a></sup> As a result of its conscription programme, the IDF maintains approximately 176,500 active troops and an additional 465,000 reservists, giving Israel one of the world's highest <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_number_of_military_and_paramilitary_personnel" title="List of countries by number of military and paramilitary personnel">percentage of citizens with military training</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-IISS_military_543-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-IISS_military-543">&#91;536&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:IDF_Air_Defense_fighters_during_Operation_Guardian_of_the_Walls,_May_2021._I.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/36/IDF_Air_Defense_fighters_during_Operation_Guardian_of_the_Walls%2C_May_2021._I.jpg/220px-IDF_Air_Defense_fighters_during_Operation_Guardian_of_the_Walls%2C_May_2021._I.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="148" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/36/IDF_Air_Defense_fighters_during_Operation_Guardian_of_the_Walls%2C_May_2021._I.jpg/330px-IDF_Air_Defense_fighters_during_Operation_Guardian_of_the_Walls%2C_May_2021._I.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/36/IDF_Air_Defense_fighters_during_Operation_Guardian_of_the_Walls%2C_May_2021._I.jpg/440px-IDF_Air_Defense_fighters_during_Operation_Guardian_of_the_Walls%2C_May_2021._I.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2000" data-file-height="1346" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Iron_Dome" title="Iron Dome">Iron Dome</a> is the world's first operational anti-<a href="/wiki/Rocket_artillery" title="Rocket artillery">artillery rocket</a> defense system.</figcaption></figure>
<p>The nation's military relies heavily on high-tech <a href="/wiki/Military_equipment_of_Israel" class="mw-redirect" title="Military equipment of Israel">weapons</a> systems <a href="/wiki/Defense_industry_of_Israel" title="Defense industry of Israel">designed and manufactured in Israel</a> as well as some foreign imports. The <a href="/wiki/Arrow_(Israeli_missile)" class="mw-redirect" title="Arrow (Israeli missile)">Arrow</a> missile is one of the world's few operational <a href="/wiki/Anti-ballistic_missile" title="Anti-ballistic missile">anti-ballistic missile</a> systems.<sup id="cite_ref-544" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-544">&#91;537&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Python_(missile)" title="Python (missile)">Python</a> air-to-air missile series is often considered one of the most crucial weapons in its military history.<sup id="cite_ref-545" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-545">&#91;538&#93;</a></sup> Israel's <a href="/wiki/Spike_(missile)" title="Spike (missile)">Spike</a> missile is one of the most widely exported <a href="/wiki/Anti-tank_guided_missile" title="Anti-tank guided missile">anti-tank guided missiles</a> (ATGMs) in the world.<sup id="cite_ref-546" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-546">&#91;539&#93;</a></sup> Israel's <a href="/wiki/Iron_Dome" title="Iron Dome">Iron Dome</a> anti-missile air defense system gained worldwide acclaim after intercepting hundreds of <a href="/wiki/Qassam_rocket" title="Qassam rocket">Qassam</a>, <a href="/wiki/BM-21_Grad" title="BM-21 Grad">122 mm Grad</a> and <a href="/wiki/Fajr-5" title="Fajr-5">Fajr-5</a> artillery <a href="/wiki/Palestinian_rocket_attacks_on_Israel" title="Palestinian rocket attacks on Israel">rockets fire by Palestinian militants</a> from the Gaza Strip.<sup id="cite_ref-Johnson_547-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Johnson-547">&#91;540&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Tory_548-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Tory-548">&#91;541&#93;</a></sup> Since the <a href="/wiki/Yom_Kippur_War" title="Yom Kippur War">Yom Kippur War</a>, Israel has developed a network of <a href="/wiki/Reconnaissance_satellites" class="mw-redirect" title="Reconnaissance satellites">reconnaissance satellites</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-549" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-549">&#91;542&#93;</a></sup> The success of the <i><a href="/wiki/Ofeq" title="Ofeq">Ofeq</a></i> programme has made Israel <a href="/wiki/Timeline_of_first_orbital_launches_by_country" title="Timeline of first orbital launches by country">one of seven countries</a> capable of launching such satellites.<sup id="cite_ref-550" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-550">&#91;543&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Israel is widely believed to <a href="/wiki/Nuclear_weapons_and_Israel" title="Nuclear weapons and Israel">possess nuclear weapons</a><sup id="cite_ref-551" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-551">&#91;544&#93;</a></sup> and per a 1993 report, chemical and biological <a href="/wiki/Israel_and_weapons_of_mass_destruction" title="Israel and weapons of mass destruction">weapons of mass destruction</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-552" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-552">&#91;545&#93;</a></sup><sup class="noprint Inline-Template" style="margin-left:0.1em; white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Dates_and_numbers#Chronological_items" title="Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers"><span title="The text near this tag is dated. (November 2021)">needs update</span></a></i>&#93;</sup> Israel has not signed the <a href="/wiki/Treaty_on_the_Non-Proliferation_of_Nuclear_Weapons" title="Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons">Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons</a><sup id="cite_ref-553" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-553">&#91;546&#93;</a></sup> and maintains a <a href="/wiki/Policy_of_deliberate_ambiguity" title="Policy of deliberate ambiguity">policy of deliberate ambiguity</a> toward its nuclear capabilities.<sup id="cite_ref-554" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-554">&#91;547&#93;</a></sup> The Israeli Navy's <a href="/wiki/Dolphin-class_submarine" title="Dolphin-class submarine">Dolphin submarines</a> are believed to be armed with nuclear <a href="/wiki/Popeye_Turbo" class="mw-redirect" title="Popeye Turbo">Popeye Turbo</a> missiles, offering <a href="/wiki/Second_strike" title="Second strike">second-strike</a> capability.<sup id="cite_ref-555" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-555">&#91;548&#93;</a></sup> Since the <a href="/wiki/Gulf_War" title="Gulf War">Gulf War</a> in 1991, when Israel was attacked by <a href="/wiki/Al_Hussein_(missile)" class="mw-redirect" title="Al Hussein (missile)">Iraqi Scud missiles</a>, all homes in Israel are required to have a reinforced security room, <a href="/wiki/Merkhav_Mugan" title="Merkhav Mugan">Merkhav Mugan</a>, impermeable to chemical and biological substances.<sup id="cite_ref-556" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-556">&#91;549&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Since Israel's establishment, military expenditure constituted a significant portion of the country's <a href="/wiki/Gross_domestic_product" title="Gross domestic product">gross domestic product</a>, with peak of 30.3% of GDP spent on defense in 1975.<sup id="cite_ref-557" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-557">&#91;550&#93;</a></sup> In 2021, Israel ranked 15th in the world <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_military_expenditures" title="List of countries by military expenditures">by total military expenditure</a>, with $24.3 billion, and 6th by defense spending as a percentage of GDP, with 5.2%.<sup id="cite_ref-558" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-558">&#91;551&#93;</a></sup> Since 1974, the United States has been a particularly notable contributor of <a href="/wiki/Israel%E2%80%93United_States_military_relations#Military_aid_and_procurement" title="Israel–United States military relations">military aid to Israel</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-559" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-559">&#91;552&#93;</a></sup> Under a <a href="/wiki/Memorandum_of_understanding" title="Memorandum of understanding">memorandum of understanding</a> signed in 2016, the U.S. is expected to provide the country with $3.8&#160;billion per year, or around 20% of Israel's defense budget, from 2018 to 2028.<sup id="cite_ref-560" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-560">&#91;553&#93;</a></sup> Israel ranked 9th globally for <a href="/wiki/Arms_industry" title="Arms industry">arms exports</a> in 2022.<sup id="cite_ref-561" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-561">&#91;554&#93;</a></sup> The majority of Israel's arms exports are unreported for security reasons.<sup id="cite_ref-562" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-562">&#91;555&#93;</a></sup> Israel is consistently rated low in the <a href="/wiki/Global_Peace_Index" title="Global Peace Index">Global Peace Index</a>, ranking 134th out of 163 nations for peacefulness in 2022.<sup id="cite_ref-GPI_563-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-GPI-563">&#91;556&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Economy">Economy</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Economy_of_Israel" title="Economy of Israel">Economy of Israel</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Ayalon_Highway,_Tel_Aviv_(cropped).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c0/Ayalon_Highway%2C_Tel_Aviv_%28cropped%29.jpg/220px-Ayalon_Highway%2C_Tel_Aviv_%28cropped%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="170" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c0/Ayalon_Highway%2C_Tel_Aviv_%28cropped%29.jpg/330px-Ayalon_Highway%2C_Tel_Aviv_%28cropped%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c0/Ayalon_Highway%2C_Tel_Aviv_%28cropped%29.jpg/440px-Ayalon_Highway%2C_Tel_Aviv_%28cropped%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3424" data-file-height="2644" /></a><figcaption>The <a href="/wiki/Diamond_Exchange_District" title="Diamond Exchange District">Diamond Exchange District</a> in <a href="/wiki/Ramat_Gan" title="Ramat Gan">Ramat Gan</a></figcaption></figure>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Tel_Aviv_Stock_Exchange_-_New_Building_Lobby_1.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e4/Tel_Aviv_Stock_Exchange_-_New_Building_Lobby_1.jpg/220px-Tel_Aviv_Stock_Exchange_-_New_Building_Lobby_1.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="163" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e4/Tel_Aviv_Stock_Exchange_-_New_Building_Lobby_1.jpg/330px-Tel_Aviv_Stock_Exchange_-_New_Building_Lobby_1.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e4/Tel_Aviv_Stock_Exchange_-_New_Building_Lobby_1.jpg/440px-Tel_Aviv_Stock_Exchange_-_New_Building_Lobby_1.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4208" data-file-height="3120" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Tel_Aviv_Stock_Exchange" title="Tel Aviv Stock Exchange">Tel Aviv Stock Exchange</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>Israel is considered the most advanced country in <a href="/wiki/Western_Asia" class="mw-redirect" title="Western Asia">Western Asia</a> and the Middle East in economic and industrial development.<sup id="cite_ref-Chua_2003_219–220_564-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Chua_2003_219–220-564">&#91;557&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-565" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-565">&#91;558&#93;</a></sup> In recent years Israel has had the highest growth rate in the Western world along with <a href="/wiki/Republic_of_Ireland" title="Republic of Ireland">Ireland</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-566" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-566">&#91;559&#93;</a></sup> In 2023, the IMF estimated Israel's GDP at 564 billion dollars and Israel's GDP per capita at 58,270 (<a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_GDP_(nominal)_per_capita" title="List of countries by GDP (nominal) per capita">ranking 13rd worldwide</a>), a figure comparable to other highly developed and rich countries.<sup id="cite_ref-567" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-567">&#91;560&#93;</a></sup> Israel has the highest average <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_wealth_per_adult" title="List of countries by wealth per adult">wealth per adult</a> in the Middle East.<sup id="cite_ref-CS_2019-1_568-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-CS_2019-1-568">&#91;561&#93;</a></sup> <i><a href="/wiki/The_Economist" title="The Economist">The Economist</a></i> ranked Israel as the 4th most successful economy among the developed countries for 2022.<sup id="cite_ref-569" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-569">&#91;562&#93;</a></sup> It has the highest number of <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_number_of_billionaires" title="List of countries by number of billionaires">billionaires in the Middle East</a> ranked 18th.<sup id="cite_ref-570" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-570">&#91;563&#93;</a></sup> Israel's quality <a href="/wiki/List_of_universities_and_colleges_in_Israel" class="mw-redirect" title="List of universities and colleges in Israel">university education</a> and the establishment of a highly motivated and educated populace is largely responsible for spurring the country's high technology boom and rapid economic development.<sup id="cite_ref-David_Adler_369-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-David_Adler-369">&#91;362&#93;</a></sup> In 2010, it joined the <a href="/wiki/OECD" title="OECD">OECD</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-OECD_30-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-OECD-30">&#91;24&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-571" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-571">&#91;564&#93;</a></sup> The country is ranked 20th in the <a href="/wiki/World_Economic_Forum" title="World Economic Forum">World Economic Forum</a>'s <i><a href="/wiki/Global_Competitiveness_Report" title="Global Competitiveness Report">Global Competitiveness Report</a></i><sup id="cite_ref-rank_2019_572-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-rank_2019-572">&#91;565&#93;</a></sup> and 35th on the <a href="/wiki/World_Bank" title="World Bank">World Bank</a>'s <a href="/wiki/Ease_of_doing_business_index" title="Ease of doing business index"><i>Ease of Doing Business</i> index</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-573" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-573">&#91;566&#93;</a></sup> Israel was also ranked fifth in the world by share of people in high-skilled employment.<sup id="cite_ref-574" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-574">&#91;567&#93;</a></sup> Israeli economic data covers the economic territory of Israel, including the Golan Heights, East Jerusalem and Israeli settlements in the West Bank.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEOECD2011_417-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEOECD2011-417">&#91;410&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Despite limited natural resources, intensive development of the <a href="/wiki/Agriculture_in_Israel" title="Agriculture in Israel">agricultural</a> and industrial sectors over the past decades has made Israel largely self-sufficient in food production, apart from grains and beef. Imports to Israel, totaling $96.5&#160;billion in 2020, include raw materials, military equipment, investment goods, rough diamonds, fuels, grain, and consumer goods.<sup id="cite_ref-cia_280-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cia-280">&#91;273&#93;</a></sup> Leading exports include machinery and equipment, software, <a href="/wiki/Diamond_industry_in_Israel" title="Diamond industry in Israel">cut diamonds</a>, agricultural products, chemicals, and textiles and apparel; in 2020, Israeli exports reached $114&#160;billion.<sup id="cite_ref-cia_280-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cia-280">&#91;273&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Bank_of_Israel" title="Bank of Israel">Bank of Israel</a> holds $201 billion of <a href="/wiki/Foreign-exchange_reserves" class="mw-redirect" title="Foreign-exchange reserves">foreign-exchange reserves</a>, the 17th highest in the world.<sup id="cite_ref-cia_280-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cia-280">&#91;273&#93;</a></sup> Since the 1970s, Israel has received <a href="/wiki/Israel%E2%80%93United_States_military_relations" title="Israel–United States military relations">military aid</a> from the United States, as well as economic assistance in the form of <a href="/wiki/Loan_guarantee" title="Loan guarantee">loan guarantees</a>, which now account for roughly half of Israel's <a href="/wiki/External_debt" title="External debt">external debt</a>. Israel has <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_external_debt" title="List of countries by external debt">one of the lowest</a> external debts in the developed world, and is a lender in terms of net external debt (<a href="/wiki/Net_international_investment_position" title="Net international investment position">assets vs. liabilities abroad</a>), which in 2015<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Israel&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup> stood at a surplus of $69&#160;billion.<sup id="cite_ref-575" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-575">&#91;568&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Israel has the second-largest number of <a href="/wiki/Startup_company" title="Startup company">startup companies</a> in the world after the United States,<sup id="cite_ref-576" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-576">&#91;569&#93;</a></sup> and the third-largest number of <a href="/wiki/List_of_Israeli_companies_quoted_on_the_Nasdaq" class="mw-redirect" title="List of Israeli companies quoted on the Nasdaq">NASDAQ-listed companies</a> after the U.S. and China.<sup id="cite_ref-577" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-577">&#91;570&#93;</a></sup> It is the world leader for number of start-ups per capita.<sup id="cite_ref-578" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-578">&#91;571&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Intel" title="Intel">Intel</a><sup id="cite_ref-579" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-579">&#91;572&#93;</a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/Microsoft" title="Microsoft">Microsoft</a><sup id="cite_ref-580" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-580">&#91;573&#93;</a></sup> built their first overseas <a href="/wiki/Research_and_development" title="Research and development">research and development</a> facilities in Israel, and other high-tech multi-national corporations, such as <a href="/wiki/IBM" title="IBM">IBM</a>, <a href="/wiki/Google" title="Google">Google</a>, <a href="/wiki/Apple_Inc." title="Apple Inc.">Apple</a>, <a href="/wiki/Hewlett-Packard" title="Hewlett-Packard">Hewlett-Packard</a>, <a href="/wiki/Cisco_Systems" class="mw-redirect" title="Cisco Systems">Cisco Systems</a>, <a href="/wiki/Facebook" title="Facebook">Facebook</a> and <a href="/wiki/Motorola" title="Motorola">Motorola</a> have opened <a href="/wiki/List_of_multinational_companies_with_research_and_development_centres_in_Israel" title="List of multinational companies with research and development centres in Israel">research and development centres in the country</a>. In 2007, American investor <a href="/wiki/Warren_Buffett" title="Warren Buffett">Warren Buffett</a>'s holding company <a href="/wiki/Berkshire_Hathaway" title="Berkshire Hathaway">Berkshire Hathaway</a> bought the Israeli company <a href="/wiki/Iscar" class="mw-redirect" title="Iscar">Iscar</a> for $4&#160;billion, its first <a href="/wiki/List_of_assets_owned_by_Berkshire_Hathaway" title="List of assets owned by Berkshire Hathaway">acquisition</a> outside the United States.<sup id="cite_ref-581" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-581">&#91;574&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The days which are allocated to working times in Israel are Sunday through Thursday (for a five-day <a href="/wiki/Workweek" class="mw-redirect" title="Workweek">workweek</a>), or Friday (for a six-day workweek). In observance of <i><a href="/wiki/Shabbat" title="Shabbat">Shabbat</a></i>, in places where Friday is a work day and the majority of population is Jewish, Friday is a "short day", usually lasting until 14:00 in the winter, or 16:00 in the summer. Several proposals have been raised to adjust the work week with the majority of the world, and make Sunday a non-working day, while extending working time of other days or replacing Friday with Sunday as a work day.<sup id="cite_ref-582" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-582">&#91;575&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Science_and_technology">Science and technology</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Science_and_technology_in_Israel" title="Science and technology in Israel">Science and technology in Israel</a> and <a href="/wiki/List_of_Israeli_inventions_and_discoveries" title="List of Israeli inventions and discoveries">List of Israeli inventions and discoveries</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Matam_hi-tech_park_(Haifa).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7f/Matam_hi-tech_park_%28Haifa%29.jpg/220px-Matam_hi-tech_park_%28Haifa%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="159" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7f/Matam_hi-tech_park_%28Haifa%29.jpg/330px-Matam_hi-tech_park_%28Haifa%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7f/Matam_hi-tech_park_%28Haifa%29.jpg/440px-Matam_hi-tech_park_%28Haifa%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2200" data-file-height="1589" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Matam,_Haifa" title="Matam, Haifa">Matam</a> high-tech park in Haifa</figcaption></figure>
<p>Israel's development of cutting-edge technologies in software, communications and the life sciences have <a href="/wiki/Silicon_Wadi" title="Silicon Wadi">evoked comparisons</a> with <a href="/wiki/Silicon_Valley" title="Silicon Valley">Silicon Valley</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-583" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-583">&#91;576&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-584" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-584">&#91;577&#93;</a></sup> Israel is first in the world in <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_research_and_development_spending" class="mw-redirect" title="List of countries by research and development spending">expenditure on research and development</a> as a percentage of GDP.<sup id="cite_ref-OECD_R&amp;D_585-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-OECD_R&amp;D-585">&#91;578&#93;</a></sup> It is ranked sixteenth in the <a href="/wiki/Global_Innovation_Index" title="Global Innovation Index">Global Innovation Index</a> in 2022, down from tenth in 2019 and fifth in the 2019 <a href="/wiki/Bloomberg_Innovation_Index" class="mw-redirect" title="Bloomberg Innovation Index">Bloomberg Innovation Index</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-586" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-586">&#91;579&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-587" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-587">&#91;580&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-588" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-588">&#91;581&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-589" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-589">&#91;582&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-590" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-590">&#91;583&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Bloomberg_innovation_591-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Bloomberg_innovation-591">&#91;584&#93;</a></sup> Israel has 140 scientists, technicians, and engineers per 10,000 employees, the highest number in the world, for comparison the U.S. has 85 per 100,000.<sup id="cite_ref-592" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-592">&#91;585&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-593" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-593">&#91;586&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-594" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-594">&#91;587&#93;</a></sup> Israel has produced six <a href="/wiki/List_of_Israeli_Nobel_laureates" title="List of Israeli Nobel laureates">Nobel Prize-winning</a> scientists since 2004<sup id="cite_ref-nobel_595-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-nobel-595">&#91;588&#93;</a></sup> and has been frequently ranked as one of the countries with the highest ratios of <a href="/wiki/Scientific_papers" class="mw-redirect" title="Scientific papers">scientific papers</a> per capita in the world.<sup id="cite_ref-596" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-596">&#91;589&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-597" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-597">&#91;590&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-598" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-598">&#91;591&#93;</a></sup> Israel has led the world in <a href="/wiki/Stem_cell" title="Stem cell">stem-cell</a> research papers per capita since 2000.<sup id="cite_ref-scell_599-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-scell-599">&#91;592&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/List_of_Israeli_universities_and_colleges" title="List of Israeli universities and colleges">Israeli universities</a> are ranked among the top 50 world universities in computer science (<a href="/wiki/Technion" class="mw-redirect" title="Technion">Technion</a> and <a href="/wiki/Tel_Aviv_University"
